vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine 'one' (一) arrow going 'straight' (直) ahead, never turning = continuously.
vocabulary.etymology: 一 (one) + 直 (straight). Literally 'one straight line,' extended to mean continuous.

examples.pinyin: Yǔ yīzhí xià.
examples.english: It's been raining continuously.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yīzhí zài děng nǐ.
examples.english: I've been waiting for you all along.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes an action/state persists from past to present.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'One' (一) kind, 'kind' (般) = all of the same kind, nothing special.
vocabulary.etymology: 一 (one) + 般 (sort, kind). Originally meant 'one kind,' now means 'ordinary' or 'in general.'

examples.pinyin: Zhège diànyǐng yībān.
examples.english: This movie is just so-so.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yībān liù diǎn qǐchuáng.
examples.english: I generally get up at six.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can mean 'average/mediocre' or 'usually/in general' depending on context.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Wishing you 'peace' (平安) all along 'the way' (一路).
vocabulary.etymology: 一路 (one road, the whole journey) + 平安 (safe and sound). A common farewell blessing.

examples.pinyin: Zàijiàn, yīlù píng'ān!
examples.english: Goodbye, have a safe trip!

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yīlù píng'ān.
examples.english: Wishing you a safe journey.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common farewell said to someone embarking on a trip.

vocabulary.mnemonic: May you have 'smooth wind' (顺风) at your back all 'the way' (一路).
vocabulary.etymology: 一路 (one road, the whole journey) + 顺风 (favorable wind). Derived from sailing blessings.

examples.chinese: 飞机要起飞了，一路顺风！
examples.pinyin: Fēijī yào qǐfēi le, yīlù shùnfēng!
examples.english: The plane is about to take off, have a smooth flight!

examples.chinese: 他开车去北京，我们祝他一路顺风。
examples.pinyin: Tā kāichē qù Běijīng, wǒmen zhù tā yīlù shùnfēng.
examples.english: He's driving to Beijing, we wish him a smooth trip.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to '一路平安,' often used for flights or long-distance travel.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'One' (一) 'part' (部分) of the whole cake.
vocabulary.etymology: 一 (one) + 部分 (part). A straightforward compound.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ chī le yī bùfen.
examples.english: I only ate a portion of it.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī bùfen yuányīn.
examples.english: This is one part of the reason.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to indicate a segment or fraction of a whole.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine ten thousand scorpions (the character 万 looks a bit like one!).
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 萬 (ten thousand). The original character 萬 was a pictograph of a scorpion, later borrowed for the number.

examples.pinyin: Zhège chéngshì yǒu yī wàn rén.
examples.english: This city has ten thousand people.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie!
examples.english: Thanks a million! (lit. ten thousand thanks)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also used figuratively to mean 'a great number' or 'very.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Above' (上) this week = last week.
vocabulary.etymology: 上 (upper, previous) + 周 (week). Time flows 'up' (past) and 'down' (future) in Chinese metaphor.

examples.pinyin: Shàng zhōu wǒ qù kàn diànyǐng le.
examples.english: I went to see a movie last week.

examples.pinyin: Shàng zhōu de tiānqì hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The weather was very good last week.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the calendar week immediately before the current one.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Below' (下) this week = next week.
vocabulary.etymology: 下 (lower, next) + 周 (week).

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xià zhōu jiàn.
examples.english: See you next week.

examples.pinyin: Xià zhōu wǒ yǒu yīgè kǎoshì.
examples.english: I have an exam next week.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the calendar week immediately after the current one.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Down' (下) comes 'snow' (雪).
vocabulary.etymology: 下 (to fall down) + 雪 (snow). A verb-object compound describing the natural phenomenon.

examples.pinyin: Wàimiàn xià xuě le!
examples.english: It's snowing outside!

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān xià le hěn dà de xuě.
examples.english: It snowed heavily yesterday.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common subjectless verb phrase. The subject (sky/heaven) is usually omitted.

vocabulary.english: in a little while; soon after
vocabulary.mnemonic: Literally 'not one moment' (一会儿) = in no time at all.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 一会儿 (a short while).

examples.pinyin: Tā bù yīhuǐr jiù huílái le.
examples.english: He came back after just a little while.

examples.pinyin: Bù yīhuǐr, cài jiù shàng lái le.
examples.english: The food arrived shortly after.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Indicates a short duration between events. Often used in storytelling.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Not' (不) 'definite' (一定).
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 一定 (definite, certain).

examples.pinyin: Tā bù yīdìng lái.
examples.english: He might not come.

examples.chinese: 便宜的东西不一定不好。
examples.pinyin: Piányi de dōngxī bù yīdìng bù hǎo.
examples.english: Cheap things aren't necessarily bad.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to express uncertainty or to disagree with an assumption.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Not' (不) a 'long' (久) time.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 久 (a long time).

examples.pinyin: Tā bùjiǔ jiù zǒu le.
examples.english: He left soon after.

examples.pinyin: Bùjiǔ yǐhòu wǒmen zài jiànmiàn.
examples.english: Let's meet again before long.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a short time in the past or future from a reference point.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Starts a sentence, meaning 'this is NOT ALL' (不但).
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 但 (but, only). Literally 'not only.'

examples.chinese: 他不但会说英语，还会说汉语。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùdàn huì shuō Yīngyǔ, hái huì shuō Hànyǔ.
examples.english: He can speak not only English but also Chinese.

examples.chinese: 她不但聪明，而且很努力。
examples.pinyin: Tā bùdàn cōngmíng, érqiě hěn nǔlì.
examples.english: She is not only smart but also very hardworking.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Always used with '而且', '还', or '也' in the second clause.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Not' (不) 'same' (同).
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 同 (same).

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen de xiǎngfǎ bùtóng.
examples.english: Our ways of thinking are different.

examples.chinese: 每个地方的文化都不同。
examples.pinyin: Měi gè dìfāng de wénhuà dōu bùtóng.
examples.english: The culture of every place is different.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to compare two or more things.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Not' (不) 'sufficient' (够).
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 够 (enough, sufficient).

examples.pinyin: Qián bùgòu.
examples.english: There's not enough money.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ juéde nǐ bùgòu nǔlì.
examples.english: I think you're not trying hard enough.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often follows the subject or object it describes (e.g., 时间不够).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Not' (不) 'too' (太) much.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 太 (too, very).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù tài xǐhuan zhège yánsè.
examples.english: I don't really like this color.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān bù tài lěng.
examples.english: It's not too cold today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Softens a negative statement, making it less absolute.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your face is 'not good to look at' because you're embarrassed or apologetic.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 好 (good) + 意思 (meaning, idea). Literally 'not good meaning,' implying awkwardness.

examples.pinyin: Bù hǎoyìsi, wǒ lái wǎn le.
examples.english: Sorry I'm late.

examples.chinese: 他收到礼物，不好意思地笑了。
examples.pinyin: Tā shōu dào lǐwù, bù hǎoyìsi de xiào le.
examples.english: He received the gift and smiled sheepishly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Multipurpose: mild apology, to get attention politely, or to express shyness.

vocabulary.english: not as good as; better to
vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Not' (不) 'equal to' (如) = inferior to.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 如 (to be like, equal to).

examples.pinyin: Zuò dìtiě bùrú qí chē kuài.
examples.english: Taking the subway is not as fast as biking.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bùrú qù kàn diànyǐng ba.
examples.english: We'd better go see a movie.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for comparison (A不如B) or to suggest a preferable alternative (不如 + suggestion).

vocabulary.english: many; quite a few; not few
vocabulary.mnemonic: The opposite of 不少 is 'few.' If it's 'not few,' it's many.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 少 (few).

examples.pinyin: Tā kàn le bù shǎo shū.
examples.english: He has read quite a few books.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān lái le bù shǎo rén.
examples.english: Quite a few people came today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Indicates a number or quantity that is above average or expectation.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your heart is 'not' (不) 'full' (满) = unsatisfied.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 满 (full, satisfied).

examples.chinese: 他对这个结果非常不满。
examples.pinyin: Tā duì zhège jiéguǒ fēicháng bùmǎn.
examples.english: He is very dissatisfied with this result.

examples.pinyin: Gùkè de bùmǎn qíngxù.
examples.english: The customer's feelings of discontent.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with 对 (duì) to indicate the target of dissatisfaction.

vocabulary.english: won't do; not okay; no good
vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Not' (不) allowed to 'go' (行) = not permissible.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 行 (to go, to be okay).

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān bù xíng, wǒ yǒu shì.
examples.english: Tomorrow won't work, I have something on.

examples.pinyin: Zhège bànfǎ bù xíng.
examples.english: This method is no good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common spoken refusal or assessment of something as unacceptable.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A strong hand saying 'NO!' (不) and 'WANT' (要) = don't want.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 要 (to want).

examples.pinyin: Bù yào shuōhuà!
examples.english: Don't talk!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù yào zhège.
examples.english: I don't want this.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for negative commands (stronger than 别) or to express not wanting something.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The argument goes 'no' (不) further than 'passing' (过) this point = but.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 过 (to pass). Originally meant 'cannot pass,' now used for transition.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, bùguò tài máng le.
examples.english: I'd like to go, but I'm too busy.

examples.pinyin: Tā bùguò shì gè háizi.
examples.english: He's just a child.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a conjunction, it's slightly softer than '但是.' As an adverb, it means 'only' or 'merely.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'Not' (不) 'wrong' (错) = correct, good.
vocabulary.etymology: 不 (not) + 错 (wrong, mistake).

examples.pinyin: Zhège cài wèidào bùcuò.
examples.english: This dish tastes pretty good.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò dé bùcuò.
examples.english: You did a good job.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common, positive but not emphatic compliment. Means 'quite good.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: 'East' (东) 'north' (北) direction.
vocabulary.etymology: 东 (east) + 北 (north). A cardinal direction compound.

examples.pinyin: Fēng cóng dōngběi fāngxiàng lái.
examples.english: The wind is coming from the northeast.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de lǎojiā zài Dōngběi.
examples.english: My hometown is in Northeast China.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to the geographical direction or specifically to the region of Northeast China.

vocabulary.mnemonic: '一' (one) + '共' (together) = All together as ONE total.
vocabulary.etymology: '一'表示整体，'共'表示'共同、合计'。

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yīgòng wǔ gè rén.
examples.english: There are five of us altogether.

examples.pinyin: Zhèxiē dōngxi yīgòng duōshǎo qián?
examples.english: How much are all these things in total?

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用在数量词前面，表示总和。比'总共'更口语化。

vocabulary.mnemonic: '一点' (a dot) 再加'点' (dot) = 更小更小的一点点。
vocabulary.etymology: '一点'表示少量，叠用'点点'起强调作用，表示极少。

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ chī yīdiǎndiǎn.
examples.english: I'll only eat a tiny bit.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒudiǎn lèi.
examples.english: I'm a little tired. (对比 '一点点累' 更常说 '有点累')

vocabulary.usage_notes: '一点'和'一点点'都表示少量，'一点点'程度更轻，语气更可爱或更强调少。通常用在肯定句。否定句一般用'一点也/都不...'。

vocabulary.mnemonic: '一' (one) + '生' (life) = ONE whole LIFE.
vocabulary.etymology: 字面意思为'从出生到死亡的一辈子'。

examples.chinese: 这是我一生中最美好的回忆。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ yīshēng zhōng zuì měihǎo de huíyì.
examples.english: This is the best memory of my whole life.

examples.chinese: 她一生都住在这个小镇。
examples.pinyin: Tā yīshēng dōu zhù zài zhège xiǎo zhèn.
examples.english: She lived in this small town her entire life.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 书面和口语都用，但比'一辈子'稍微书面一点。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Combine the directions 东 (east) and 南 (south).
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 东 (east) and 南 (south), literally "east-south".

examples.chinese: 我家住在北京的东南边。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zhù zài Běijīng de dōng nán biān.
examples.english: My home is in the southeast of Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Fēng cóng dōng nán fāng xiàng chuī guò lái.
examples.english: The wind is blowing from the southeast.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used like "southwest" or "northeast".

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of the sun (日) rising in the East (东).
vocabulary.etymology: 东 (east) + 方 (direction, side).

examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng cóng Dōng fāng shēng qǐ.
examples.english: The sun rises in the east.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xǐhuān Dōng fāng yìshù.
examples.english: I really like Eastern art.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Capitalized when referring to the cultural/political East vs. West (Dōng fāng).

vocabulary.mnemonic: How 'individual' (个) you are in terms of height.
vocabulary.etymology: 个 (individual unit) + 子 (noun suffix). It describes the stature of a single person.

examples.pinyin: Tā gèzi hěn gāo.
examples.english: He is very tall.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ dìdi gèzi duō gāo le?
examples.english: How tall is your younger brother now?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to ask or comment on a person's height.

vocabulary.mnemonic: "Middle Medicine" — from the center (中) of Chinese culture.
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (China, central) + 医 (medicine).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yéye xiāngxìn Zhōng yī.
examples.english: My grandpa believes in Traditional Chinese Medicine.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ kànguò Zhōng yī ma?
examples.english: Have you ever seen a TCM doctor?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the medical system, not just a doctor (though '中医师' is more precise for the practitioner).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Combines 中 (middle) school and 小 (small/elementary) school.
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (middle) + 小 (small) + 学 (school).

examples.pinyin: Zhōng xiǎo xué shēng dōu yào chuān xiàofú.
examples.english: All primary and secondary school students must wear uniforms.

examples.chinese: 这是给中小学生读的书。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gěi zhōng xiǎo xué shēng dú de shū.
examples.english: This is a book for primary and secondary school students to read.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the entire K-12 stage before university.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'middle' (中) of your 'years' (年).
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (middle) + 年 (year).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba yǐjīng dào zhōng nián le.
examples.english: My dad has already reached middle age.

examples.chinese: 这是一部关于中年人的电影。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī bù guānyú zhōng nián rén de diànyǐng.
examples.english: This is a movie about middle-aged people.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'heart' (心) in the 'middle' (中).
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (middle) + 心 (heart). The core or heart of something.

examples.chinese: 人民广场是上海的中心。
examples.pinyin: Rénmín Guǎngchǎng shì Shànghǎi de zhōng xīn.
examples.english: People's Square is the center of Shanghai.

examples.pinyin: Tǎolùn de zhōng xīn shì shénme?
examples.english: What is the main point of the discussion?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be physical (city center) or abstract (the core idea).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Middle (中) grade/level (级).
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (middle) + 级 (level, grade).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ Hànyǔ shì zhōng jí shuǐpíng.
examples.english: My Chinese is at an intermediate level.

examples.chinese: 这个班适合中级学习者。
examples.pinyin: Zhège bān shìhé zhōng jí xuéxí zhě.
examples.english: This class is suitable for intermediate learners.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for language proficiency, courses, or exams.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Food (餐) from the Middle Kingdom (中).
vocabulary.etymology: 中 (China) + 餐 (meal, food).

examples.chinese: 今晚你想吃中餐还是西餐？
examples.pinyin: Jīn wǎn nǐ xiǎng chī zhōng cān háishì xī cān?
examples.english: Do you want to eat Chinese or Western food tonight?

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de zhōng cān hěn hǎochī.
examples.english: The Chinese food at this restaurant is delicious.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Contrasts with 西餐 (Western food).

vocabulary.english: to be / to act as / for (wéi); for the sake of (wèi)
vocabulary.mnemonic: The versatile character with two tones: wéi (to be) and wèi (for).
vocabulary.etymology: 古文字形像手牵象，表示劳作、作为。引申出多种含义。

examples.pinyin: Tā yǐ jiāo shū wéi shēng.
examples.english: He makes a living by teaching (lit. takes teaching as his life).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhème zuò dōu shì wèi le nǐ.
examples.english: I'm doing all this for you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Pronunciation changes meaning: wéi (to act as), wèi (for the purpose of). Watch for 为什么 (wèi shén me).

vocabulary.mnemonic: For (为 wèi) what (什么) reason?
vocabulary.etymology: 为 (for, wèi) + 什么 (what).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ wèi shénme chídào?
examples.english: Why are you late?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yě bù zhīdào wèi shénme.
examples.english: I don't know why either.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common and casual way to ask "why?".

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'main person' (主人).
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (master, main) + 人 (person).

examples.pinyin: Zhǔrén, huānyíng lái wǒ jiā!
examples.english: Host: Welcome to my home!

examples.chinese: 这是谁的小狗？它的主人呢？
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì shéi de xiǎo gǒu? Tā de zhǔrén ne?
examples.english: Whose puppy is this? Where is its owner?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to the host of a party, owner of an object/pet, or master in a master-servant context.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'main' (主) and 'important' (要) part.
vocabulary.etymology: 主 (main) + 要 (important, essential).

examples.pinyin: Zhǔyào wèntí shì qián búgòu.
examples.english: The main problem is not enough money.

examples.chinese: 他主要的工作是写代码。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhǔyào de gōngzuò shì xiě dàimǎ.
examples.english: His main job is writing code.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before nouns (主要 + noun).

vocabulary.english: to lift / to raise / to cite
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine lifting your hands (like the bottom part suggests) up high.
vocabulary.etymology: Traditional form 舉 shows hands (臼) lifting an object. Simplified form 举 is a modern simplification.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jǔ bú dòng zhège xiāngzi.
examples.english: I can't lift this box.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng jǔ ge lìzi ma?
examples.english: Can you give an example?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A versatile verb for lifting physically or citing abstractly.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Lift (举) your hand (手).
vocabulary.etymology: 举 (lift) + 手 (hand).

examples.pinyin: Yǒu wèntí qǐng jǔ shǒu.
examples.english: If you have a question, please raise your hand.

examples.chinese: 他举手想回答老师的问题。
examples.pinyin: Tā jǔ shǒu xiǎng huídá lǎoshī de wèntí.
examples.english: He raised his hand to answer the teacher's question.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A classroom and meeting essential.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Lift/initiate (举) and make it happen/go (行).
vocabulary.etymology: 举 (raise, initiate) + 行 (go, carry out).

examples.pinyin: Hūnlǐ xià ge yuè jǔ xíng.
examples.english: The wedding will be held next month.

examples.pinyin: Xuéxiào měi nián jǔ xíng yùndònghuì.
examples.english: The school holds a sports meet every year.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for formal or organized events like meetings, ceremonies, exams.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Also (也) permit/allow (许) the possibility.
vocabulary.etymology: 也 (also) + 许 (allow, permit).

examples.pinyin: Tā yěxǔ míngtiān lái.
examples.english: Maybe he'll come tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Yěxǔ nǐ shì duì de.
examples.english: Perhaps you are right.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and slightly formal alternative to 可能.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Practice (习) until it becomes a custom (惯).
vocabulary.etymology: 习 (practice) + 惯 (accustomed).

examples.pinyin: Zǎo qǐ shì wǒ de xíguàn.
examples.english: Getting up early is my habit.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xíguàn zhèlǐ de tiānqì.
examples.english: I'm not used to the weather here.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb, often used in negative (不习惯) or positive (习惯了) forms.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'matter' (事) and its 'situation' (情).
vocabulary.etymology: 事 (matter, affair) + 情 (feeling, situation). It refers to an affair with its surrounding circumstances.

examples.chinese: 我今天有很多事情要做。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān yǒu hěn duō shìqing yào zuò.
examples.english: I have a lot of things to do today.

examples.pinyin: Nà jiàn shìqing yǐjīng guòqù le.
examples.english: That matter is already in the past.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very broad, everyday word for any kind of matter, business, or happening.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character looks like a fluffy cloud with lines underneath.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of flowing clouds. The traditional form for 'cloud' is 雲 (rain 雨 + 云), while 云 is also the simplified form for 'to say'.

examples.pinyin: Tiān shàng de yún hěn piàoliang.
examples.english: The clouds in the sky are very beautiful.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān duō yún.
examples.english: It's cloudy today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Homophone with 云 (yún, to say - classical/literary). In modern context, it's mostly 'cloud'.

vocabulary.english: to hand over / to make (friends) / to intersect
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'crossing' paths and exchanging something.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts a person with crossed legs, implying crossing, intersecting, or handing over.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ zuòyè jiāo gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please hand in your homework to me.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn huì jiāo péngyou.
examples.english: He is very good at making friends.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A highly versatile verb central to many compounds.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Interact/hand over (交) your friendship (朋友).
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (to interact/hand over) + 朋友 (friend).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn gāoxìng hé nǐ jiāo péngyou.
examples.english: I'm very happy to make friends with you.

examples.chinese: 他在新学校交了很多朋友。
examples.pinyin: Tā zài xīn xuéxiào jiāo le hěn duō péngyou.
examples.english: He made many friends at his new school.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Use 和/跟...交朋友 (make friends with...).

vocabulary.english: to hand over to / to give to
vocabulary.mnemonic: Hand over (交) and give (给) it.
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (hand over) + 给 (to give).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bǎ yàoshi jiāo gěi nǐ le.
examples.english: I've handed the keys over to you.

examples.pinyin: Zhège rènwù jiāo gěi tā ba.
examples.english: Let's hand this task over to him.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in the pattern 把...交给... (bǎ ... jiāo gěi ...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Paths that 'cross and connect' (交 + 通).
vocabulary.etymology: 交 (intersect) + 通 (pass through, connect). The intersecting and flowing of people/vehicles.

examples.pinyin: Zǎoshang de jiāotōng hěn dǔ.
examples.english: The morning traffic is very heavy.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yòng shénme jiāotōng gōngjù?
examples.english: What means of transportation do you use?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the system or the state of traffic flow.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A high (高 component) and open place catching light.
vocabulary.etymology: Possibly derived from 高 (high) and 几 (table/ledge), suggesting a high, exposed place where light is prominent.

examples.pinyin: Zhège fángjiān hěn liàng.
examples.english: This room is very bright.

examples.pinyin: Tiān liàng le.
examples.english: It's dawn. / The sky is bright.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common for light, screens, colors, and dawn.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think: 出 (exit) + 发 (send forth). You 'exit and send yourself forth' on a journey.
vocabulary.etymology: 出 depicts a foot stepping out of a cavity. 发 (simplified from 發) originally depicted shooting an arrow, conveying the idea of sending forth.

examples.chinese: 我们明天早上七点出发。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān zǎoshang qī diǎn chū fā.
examples.english: We set off at 7 AM tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Kuài diǎnr, gāi chū fā le!
examples.english: Hurry up, it's time to go!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for starting trips or journeys, both long and short.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (exit) + 口 (mouth). An exit is a 'mouth' you 'go out' of.
vocabulary.etymology: 口 pictographically represents a mouth or opening. Combined with 出 (to exit), it forms the concept of an exit.

examples.pinyin: Diànyǐngyuàn chū kǒu zài nà biān.
examples.english: The cinema exit is over there.

examples.chinese: 中国出口很多电子产品。
examples.pinyin: Zhōngguó chū kǒu hěn duō diànzǐ chǎnpǐn.
examples.english: China exports a lot of electronic products.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a noun, it's the opposite of 入口 (entrance).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (exit) + 国 (country). To 'exit your country'.
vocabulary.etymology: 国 (simplified from 國) originally depicted a territory enclosed by boundaries. Combined with 出, it means to leave that territory.

examples.pinyin: Tā xià gè yuè yào chū guó gōngzuò.
examples.english: He's going abroad for work next month.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi chū guò guó ne.
examples.english: I've never been abroad.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly followed by 了 or verbs like 留学 (study abroad), 旅游 (travel abroad).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (come out) + 现 (appear). It's like something 'comes out and manifests'.
vocabulary.etymology: 现 (simplified from 現) combines 王 (jade) and 見 (see), implying something precious becoming visible.

examples.pinyin: Tàiyáng zhōngyú chū xiàn le.
examples.english: The sun finally appeared.

examples.chinese: 会议上出现了一个新想法。
examples.pinyin: Huìyì shàng chū xiàn le yī gè xīn xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: A new idea appeared at the meeting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The opposite is 消失 (disappear). Can be used for people, things, or abstract concepts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (come out) + 生 (life/birth). You 'come out' to start your 'life'.
vocabulary.etymology: 生 depicts a sprout emerging from the earth, symbolizing birth and life.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chū shēng zài Běijīng.
examples.english: I was born in Beijing.

examples.pinyin: Tā de xiǎo bǎobao gānggāng chū shēng.
examples.english: Her baby was just born.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used with 在 (zài) to indicate place of birth.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (out) + 租 (rent). To 'rent something out'.
vocabulary.etymology: 租 originally involved grain tax, later extended to mean rent. Combined with 出, it means to release for rent.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiān fángzi chū zū.
examples.english: This room is for rent.

examples.chinese: 他把自行车出租给游客。
examples.pinyin: Tā bǎ zìxíngchē chū zū gěi yóukè.
examples.english: He rents out his bicycle to tourists.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often seen on signs (e.g., 房屋出租). The renter is 租客, the landlord is 房东.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出租 (for rent) + 车 (vehicle). A 'vehicle for rent'.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound of 出租 (to rent out) and 车 (vehicle/wheeled conveyance).

examples.chinese: 我们打车（坐出租车）去吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dǎ chē (zuò chū zū chē) qù ba.
examples.english: Let's take a taxi.

examples.pinyin: Chū zū chē sījī hěn yǒuhǎo.
examples.english: The taxi driver is very friendly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Colloquially shortened to 的士 (from Cantonese) or just 车 in 打车 (to hail a taxi).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (exit) + 门 (door/gate). 'Exit the door'.
vocabulary.etymology: 门 pictographically represents a double door. Exiting the door means leaving home.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chū mén le, wǎnshang jiàn!
examples.english: I'm heading out, see you tonight!

examples.pinyin: Chū mén jìde dài sǎn.
examples.english: Remember to take an umbrella when you go out.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common phrase for leaving your house/apartment for any reason.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 出 (exit) + 院 (courtyard/hospital). 'Exit the hospital courtyard'.
vocabulary.etymology: 院 refers to a courtyard or enclosed institution. 出院 means to leave such a medical institution.

examples.pinyin: Yéye míngtiān kěyǐ chū yuàn le.
examples.english: Grandpa can be discharged from the hospital tomorrow.

examples.chinese: 她出院以后需要多休息。
examples.pinyin: Tā chū yuàn yǐhòu xūyào duō xiūxi.
examples.english: She needs to rest more after being discharged.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The opposite is 住院 (be hospitalized).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 分 (divide) + 开 (open). To 'divide and open up' a connection.
vocabulary.etymology: 分 depicts dividing something with a knife. 开 (simplified from 開) shows two hands opening a door bolt.

examples.chinese: 我们在路口分开，各走各的。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zài lùkǒu fēn kāi, gè zǒu gè de.
examples.english: We parted ways at the intersection and went our separate ways.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ hǎo de hé huài de fēn kāi.
examples.english: Please separate the good ones from the bad ones.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for people separating or for sorting/separating objects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 分 (divide/part) + 数 (number). A 'divided number' that represents your performance.
vocabulary.etymology: 数 relates to counting and numbers. Combined with 分 (a portion), it means a numerical representation of a portion achieved.

examples.chinese: 这次考试我的分数很高。
examples.pinyin: Zhè cì kǎoshì wǒ de fēn shù hěn gāo.
examples.english: I got a very high score on this exam.

examples.pinyin: Tā tài zàiyì fēn shù le.
examples.english: He cares too much about grades.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Primarily used for academic or test scores.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's a doubled word (刚 + 刚) emphasizing the immediate past.
vocabulary.etymology: 刚 means hard, strong, or just. Doubling it softens it into an adverb meaning 'just now'.

examples.pinyin: Tā gānggāng líkāi.
examples.english: He just left.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gānggāng chī wán fàn.
examples.english: I just finished eating.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Synonymous with 刚才, but 刚刚 is more colloquial. It's placed before the verb.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 到 (arrive at) + 处 (place). Arriving at every place.
vocabulary.etymology: 处 (simplified from 處) relates to a place or location. Combined with 到 (to reach), it means reaching all places.

examples.pinyin: Gōngyuán lǐ dào chù shì rén.
examples.english: There are people everywhere in the park.

examples.chinese: 我的钥匙到处都找不到。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yàoshi dào chù dōu zhǎo bù dào.
examples.english: I can't find my keys anywhere.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to emphasize the pervasiveness of something.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a clock being 'carved' into 15-minute segments.
vocabulary.etymology: The character originally depicted carving with a knife (刂) into wood. It extended to mean a notch or a mark, then a unit of time.

examples.pinyin: Xiànzài shì liǎng diǎn yī kè.
examples.english: It's a quarter past two.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài shítou shàng kè zì.
examples.english: He carves characters into the stone.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a time unit, one 刻 = 15 minutes. Often used after 点 (diǎn) for times like 三点一刻 (3:15).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 前 (before) + 年 (year). The year before (last year).
vocabulary.etymology: 前 depicts a foot in a boat moving forward, but paradoxically came to mean 'before' or 'in front'. 年 is the year.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì qián nián lái Zhōngguó de.
examples.english: I came to China the year before last.

examples.chinese: 前年夏天我们去了海边。
examples.pinyin: Qián nián xiàtiān wǒmen qù le hǎibiān.
examples.english: We went to the seaside in the summer of the year before last.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Sequence: 前年 (year before last) -> 去年 (last year) -> 今年 (this year).

vocabulary.english: to handle, to do, to manage
vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'handling' a task with force (力) and seriousness.
vocabulary.etymology: The simplified form 办 is derived from the traditional 辦, which combines 辛 (bitter, toilsome) with 分 (divide), implying managing a difficult task.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ qù bàn.
examples.english: I'll handle this matter.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xūyào bàn yī zhāng yínháng kǎ.
examples.english: I need to get a bank card.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very versatile verb for handling affairs, running errands, or organizing things.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 办 (handle work) + 公 (public/affairs) + 室 (room). A 'room for handling public/work affairs'.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound word: 办公 means 'handle official/business work' and 室 means room.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài bàn gōng shì děng nǐ.
examples.english: I'll wait for you in the office.

examples.pinyin: Tā de bàn gōng shì zài wǔ lóu.
examples.english: His office is on the fifth floor.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often abbreviated as 办 in casual work chat (e.g., 回办了吗? - Back to the office yet?).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 办 (handle) + 法 (law/method). A 'method for handling' a problem.
vocabulary.etymology: 法 originally referred to laws or models of justice. Here it means a standard method.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yī gè hǎo bàn fǎ.
examples.english: I have a good method.

examples.pinyin: Méi bàn fǎ, zhǐ néng zhèyàng le.
examples.english: There's no way, we can only do this.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used in 没办法 (there's no way/can't be helped) and 有办法 (to have a way/know-how).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of adding force (力) to your mouth (口) to speak louder? Actually, the character is based on adding force.
vocabulary.etymology: The character combines 力 (strength/force) and 口 (mouth), possibly indicating adding verbal emphasis or effort.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng gěi wǒ jiā diǎnr táng.
examples.english: Please add some sugar for me.

examples.pinyin: Zhège yuè gōngzī yòu jiā le!
examples.english: My salary increased again this month!

vocabulary.usage_notes: A fundamental verb for addition in math (加) and in everyday life (加钱, 加微信).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 加 (add) + 油 (oil/gas). Literally 'add oil'.
vocabulary.etymology: Literally means to add oil/gas to a vehicle. Figuratively, it means to put in effort/energy.

examples.pinyin: Chē méi yóu le, xūyào jiā yóu.
examples.english: The car is out of gas, it needs to refuel.

examples.pinyin: Jiā yóu! Nǐ yīdìng néng xíng!
examples.english: Come on! You can definitely do it!

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common cheer in Chinese, used like "Go!" or "You can do it!"

vocabulary.mnemonic: 动 (move) + 物 (thing). A 'moving thing'.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound word: 动 means movement, 物 means thing/creature. Hence, a creature that moves.

examples.chinese: 我最喜欢的动物是熊猫。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuan de dòng wù shì xióngmāo.
examples.english: My favorite animal is the panda.

examples.pinyin: Dòng wù yuán lǐ yǒu hěn duō dòng wù.
examples.english: There are many animals in the zoo.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The general term for all animals.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 动物 (animal) + 园 (garden/park). An 'animal park'.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound of 动物 (animal) and 园 (enclosed garden or park).

examples.chinese: 周末我们带孩子去动物园。
examples.pinyin: Zhōumò wǒmen dài háizi qù dòng wù yuán.
examples.english: We're taking the kids to the zoo on the weekend.

examples.pinyin: Zhège dòng wù yuán hěn dà.
examples.english: This zoo is very big.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 北 (north) + 方 (direction). The 'northern direction'.
vocabulary.etymology: 北 pictographically represents two people back-to-back (implying turning one's back, as in defeat, facing south). It came to mean 'north'. 方 means direction or region.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ láizì Zhōngguó de běi fāng.
examples.english: I'm from the north of China.

examples.pinyin: Běi fāng dōngtiān hěn lěng.
examples.english: Winters in the north are very cold.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often contrasted with 南方 (the south).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 十 (ten) + 分 (part). Ten out of ten parts = 100%.
vocabulary.etymology: Literally 'ten parts', meaning completely or to the fullest extent.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu shí fēn piàoliang.
examples.english: This piece of clothing is very beautiful.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ duì jiéguǒ shí fēn mǎnyì.
examples.english: I am extremely satisfied with the result.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to 非常 but can sound slightly more formal or emphatic in casual speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine the character as a person (亻) with a cross-section (十) showing a thousand layers.
vocabulary.etymology: An ancient pictogram, possibly representing a great number or multitude. It is a fundamental numeral.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tái diànnǎo wǔ qiān yuán.
examples.english: This computer is five thousand yuan.

examples.pinyin: Xièxie! Qiān yán wàn yǔ shuō bù wán.
examples.english: Thank you! A thousand words wouldn't be enough to express it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used like English 'thousand'. 两千 (liǎng qiān) is used for 'two thousand', not 二千 in modern speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think: 千 (qiān) is 'thousand' and 克 (kè) is 'gram', so it's 1000 grams.
vocabulary.etymology: A metric unit. 千 (thousand) + 克 (gram), directly translates to 'thousand grams'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le liǎng qiān kè píng guǒ.
examples.english: I bought two kilograms of apples.

examples.pinyin: Tā tǐ zhòng yǒu qī shí qiān kè.
examples.english: He weighs seventy kilograms.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In daily life, 公斤 (gōng jīn) is more common than 千克.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 午 (wǔ) is 'noon' and 睡 (shuì) is 'sleep' → sleeping at noon.
vocabulary.etymology: 午 (noon) + 睡 (sleep). Refers to the traditional rest after lunch.

examples.chinese: 我每天中午都要午睡一会儿。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zhōng wǔ dōu yào wǔ shuì yī huìr.
examples.english: I need to take a nap every noon for a while.

examples.pinyin: Bié chǎo tā, tā zài wǔ shuì ne.
examples.english: Don't disturb him, he's taking a nap.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common habit in many Chinese cultures. Can be used as a verb (去午睡) or noun (睡个午睡).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 午 (noon) + 餐 (meal) = the noon meal.
vocabulary.etymology: 午 (noon) + 餐 (meal, food).

examples.pinyin: Wǔ cān nǐ xiǎng chī shén me?
examples.english: What do you want to eat for lunch?

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī tí gōng miǎn fèi wǔ cān.
examples.english: The company provides free lunch.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 午餐 is slightly more formal than 午饭, but both are common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 半 (half) + 夜 (night) → halfway through the night.
vocabulary.etymology: Literally 'half-night', meaning the middle of the night.

examples.pinyin: Tā jīng cháng bàn yè cái huí jiā.
examples.english: He often doesn't come home until midnight.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàn yè bèi chǎo xǐng le.
examples.english: I was woken up in the middle of the night.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to mean 'very late at night', not strictly 12:00 AM.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'single position' that can be a measurement unit or your work unit.
vocabulary.etymology: 单 (single) + 位 (position, place).

examples.pinyin: Shí jiān dān wèi shì miǎo, fēn, xiǎo shí.
examples.english: Time units are seconds, minutes, and hours.

examples.chinese: 我妈妈还在原来的单位工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ mā ma hái zài yuán lái de dān wèi gōng zuò.
examples.english: My mom still works at her original workplace.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has two main meanings: 1) a standard measurement (e.g., 米); 2) one's employer or institution (especially in older systems).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The top part looks like a '十' (ten) and the bottom like a '买' (mǎi, buy) – selling things for tens (of money).
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a person selling goods in the market. The traditional form 賣 includes 貝 (shell money).

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge diàn mài shuǐ guǒ hé shū cài.
examples.english: This shop sells fruits and vegetables.

examples.chinese: 我的旧手机卖了一百块。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de jiù shǒu jī mài le yī bǎi kuài.
examples.english: I sold my old phone for 100 kuai.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Opposite of 买 (mǎi, to buy).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 南 (nán) is 'south' and 方 (fāng) is 'direction' → the southern direction.
vocabulary.etymology: 南 (south) + 方 (direction, side).

examples.chinese: 中国的南方冬天不太冷。
examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó de nán fāng dōng tiān bú tài lěng.
examples.english: South China isn't too cold in winter.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā zài chéng shì de nán fāng.
examples.english: My home is in the south of the city.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to refer to southern regions, especially in contrast to 北方.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'diviner' (卜) who 'speaks' (口) to claim a spot — occupying it.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted using a turtle shell for divination (占卜), implying establishing a position.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bié zhàn wǒ de zuò wèi.
examples.english: Please don't occupy my seat.

examples.chinese: 年轻人占公司员工的一半。
examples.pinyin: Nián qīng rén zhàn gōng sī yuán gōng de yī bàn.
examples.english: Young people constitute half of the company's staff.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 读作 'zhàn' for 'to occupy'. In '占比例', it means 'to constitute'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It looks like something blocking (卡住) a path, or a little card.
vocabulary.etymology: A pictophonetic character. Used as a phonetic loan for foreign words like 'card' (kǎ).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yòng yín háng kǎ fù qián.
examples.english: I pay with a bank card.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de diàn nǎo yòu kǎ le.
examples.english: My computer is stuck/lagging again.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has two common pronunciations and meanings: kǎ (card) and qiǎ (to get stuck, like in a machine).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 原 (original) + 因 (cause) → the original cause.
vocabulary.etymology: 原 (source, origin) + 因 (cause, reason).

examples.pinyin: Tā méi lái de yuán yīn shì shén me?
examples.english: What is the reason he didn't come?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù qīng chu jù tǐ yuán yīn.
examples.english: I'm not clear about the specific reason.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A formal word for 'reason', often used in explanations. Colloquially, 理由 (lǐ yóu) is also common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 参 (to join in) + 观 (to look) → joining in to look around.
vocabulary.etymology: 参 (take part) + 观 (observe). Means to observe and learn by looking.

examples.chinese: 明天我们去参观博物馆。
examples.pinyin: Míng tiān wǒ men qù cān guān bó wù guǎn.
examples.english: Tomorrow we are going to visit the museum.

examples.pinyin: Huān yíng cān guān wǒ men de xīn jiā.
examples.english: Welcome to visit our new home.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for visiting places like museums, factories, or schools for observation, not for visiting people.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It looks like a hand repeating an action.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of a right hand, extended to mean repetition or addition.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zěn me yòu chí dào le?
examples.english: Why are you late again?

examples.pinyin: Tā yòu cōng míng yòu piào liang.
examples.english: She is both smart and beautiful.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for something that has happened before (again) or to connect two adjectives (both...and...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 友 (friend) + 好 (good) → friend-good.
vocabulary.etymology: 友 (friend) + 好 (good).

examples.pinyin: Zhè lǐ de rén dōu hěn yǒu hǎo.
examples.english: The people here are all very friendly.

examples.chinese: 我们希望发展友好关系。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xī wàng fā zhǎn yǒu hǎo guān xì.
examples.english: We hope to develop friendly relations.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes people, relationships, or behavior.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine sending (发) something out from your hand.
vocabulary.etymology: The traditional 發 depicts shooting an arrow, conveying the idea of sending forth.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi tā fā le yī tiáo wēi xìn.
examples.english: I sent him a WeChat message.

examples.chinese: 公司每个月五号发工资。
examples.pinyin: Gōng sī měi ge yuè wǔ hào fā gōng zī.
examples.english: The company issues salary on the 5th of every month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely common verb for sending messages (短信/邮件), issuing things (工资), or expressing (发火).

vocabulary.mnemonic: An ear (耳) and a hand (又) — taking something by hand.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand (又) cutting off an ear (耳) as a war trophy, meaning 'to take'. Now simplified.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù yín háng qǔ diǎn qián.
examples.english: I'm going to the bank to get some money.

examples.pinyin: Gěi hái zi qǔ ge hǎo míng zi.
examples.english: Give the child a good name.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for getting something that is yours or available (取钱, 取快递, 取名字).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 取 (take/get) + 得 (get) → double getting, you obtain it.
vocabulary.etymology: 取 (take) + 得 (obtain).

examples.pinyin: Tā qǔ dé le hěn hǎo de chéng jì.
examples.english: He achieved very good results.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zhōng yú qǔ dé le lián xì.
examples.english: We finally got in touch.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for abstract achievements (成绩, 进步, 信任) or contact (联系). More formal than 得到.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 受 (receive) + 到 (arrive) → it arrives and you receive it.
vocabulary.etymology: 受 (to receive) + 到 (arrive, particle indicating result).

examples.chinese: 他的表演受到了大家的欢迎。
examples.pinyin: Tā de biǎo yǎn shòu dào le dà jiā de huān yíng.
examples.english: His performance received everyone's welcome.

examples.chinese: 他小时候受到很好的教育。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎo shí hou shòu dào hěn hǎo de jiào yù.
examples.english: He received a very good education when he was young.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for receiving abstract things like treatment, influence, education, praise, or criticism. Passive in feeling.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person (又) speaking (讠) under a roof (亠) — words can change things.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 變. The traditional form is complex, involving handling silk to change its form.

examples.pinyin: Tiān qì tū rán biàn le.
examples.english: The weather changed suddenly.

examples.pinyin: Jǐ nián méi jiàn, nǐ biàn le hǎo duō.
examples.english: I haven't seen you for years, you've changed a lot.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common verb for all kinds of change. Can be intransitive (他变了) or transitive (变魔术).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 变 (change) + 成 (become) → change and become something else.
vocabulary.etymology: 变 (change) + 成 (accomplish, become).

examples.pinyin: Shuǐ biàn chéng bīng le.
examples.english: The water turned into ice.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiǎng biàn chéng yī zhī niǎo.
examples.english: He wants to become a bird.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes the result of a transformation from one thing into another.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It looks like a box (口) wrapping words together to make a sentence.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a crooked hook, later borrowed for 'sentence'. The 口 (mouth) component suggests speech.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ shuō yī gè jù zi.
examples.english: Please say a sentence.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ xiě le liǎng jù huà.
examples.english: I only wrote two sentences (or 'two phrases').

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a measure word, it's used for sentences, lines of poetry, or sometimes remarks (几句话).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 句 (sentence) + 子 (noun suffix) → a full, concrete sentence.
vocabulary.etymology: 句 (sentence) + 子 (noun-forming suffix).

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jù zi shì shén me yì si?
examples.english: What does this sentence mean?

examples.pinyin: Qǐng yòng zhè ge cí zào ge jù zi.
examples.english: Please make a sentence using this word.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard word for a grammatical sentence. More specific than 话.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a single bird (隹) with a mouth (口) saying 'only one!'
vocabulary.etymology: Originally a pictograph of a bird, later borrowed phonetically for 'only'. The meaning 'only' is unrelated to the original pictograph.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ hē kā fēi, bù hē chá.
examples.english: I only drink coffee, not tea.

examples.pinyin: Xiàn zài jiā lǐ zhǐ wǒ yī gè rén.
examples.english: Right now I'm the only one at home.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Placed before the verb to limit the scope. Distinguish from 只 (zhī), a measure word for animals.

vocabulary.english: can only; have no choice but to
vocabulary.mnemonic: 只 (only) + 能 (can) → the only thing you *can* do.
vocabulary.etymology: 只 (only) + 能 (can, able).

examples.chinese: 车坏了，我们只能走路去。
examples.pinyin: Chē huài le, wǒ men zhǐ néng zǒu lù qù.
examples.english: The car broke down, we can only walk there.

examples.chinese: 我只能试试看，不一定成功。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ néng shì shì kàn, bù yī dìng chéng gōng.
examples.english: I can only give it a try, not sure if it'll succeed.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Expresses a limited option or a lack of alternatives.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 只 (only) + 要 (need) → you only need this one condition.
vocabulary.etymology: 只 (only) + 要 (need, require).

examples.pinyin: Zhǐ yào nǐ lái, wǒ jiù hěn gāo xìng.
examples.english: As long as you come, I'll be very happy.

examples.chinese: 只要努力，就能学好中文。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐ yào nǔ lì, jiù néng xué hǎo zhōng wén.
examples.english: As long as you work hard, you can learn Chinese well.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in the first part of a conditional sentence, often paired with 就 (jiù) in the second part.

vocabulary.english: to be called; to be named
vocabulary.mnemonic: 叫 (call) + 作 (make) → make/call it by this name.
vocabulary.etymology: 叫 (to call) + 作 (to make, to regard as).

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge cài jiào zuò 'gōng bǎo jī dīng'.
examples.english: This dish is called 'Kung Pao Chicken'.

examples.chinese: 那种现象叫作'海市蜃楼'。
examples.pinyin: Nà zhǒng xiàn xiàng jiào zuò 'hǎi shì shèn lóu'.
examples.english: That phenomenon is called a 'mirage'.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for naming or defining things. Slightly more formal/literary than just 叫. Often used in definitions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'shāng rén' is a 'person (人) who sells (商) things.'
vocabulary.etymology: 商 (shāng) originally meant 'to discuss' or 'trade,' and 人 (rén) means 'person.' Together it means a person engaged in commerce.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bàba shì gè shāng rén.
examples.english: My dad is a businessperson.

examples.pinyin: Nàge shāng rén mài shuǐguǒ.
examples.english: That merchant sells fruit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 通用词，涵盖从小贩到大公司的经营者。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a 'business (商) conversation' where you 'measure (量) things out' together.
vocabulary.etymology: 商 (shāng) here carries its sense of 'consult' or 'deliberate,' and 量 (liáng) means 'to measure' or 'calculate.' Combined, it implies measuring opinions together.

examples.chinese: 我们商量一下去哪儿吃饭。
examples.pinyin: Wǒmen shāngliang yīxià qù nǎr chī fàn.
examples.english: Let's discuss where to go eat.

examples.chinese: 这件事我要跟家人商量。
examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn shì wǒ yào gēn jiārén shāngliang.
examples.english: I need to discuss this matter with my family.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常用于非正式的、需要达成一致的场合。

vocabulary.english: (expression of surprise, agreement, realization, or sentence-final particle)
vocabulary.mnemonic: The sound you make when you're surprised or to emphasize a feeling: 'Ah!'
vocabulary.etymology: A pictophonetic character; the 口 (kǒu, mouth) radical indicates it's a sound made with the mouth.

examples.pinyin: Ā, shì nǐ a!
examples.english: Ah, it's you!

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de fēngjǐng zhēn měi a!
examples.english: The scenery here is so beautiful!

vocabulary.usage_notes: 口语高频词。随语气和语境不同，声调也会变化。

vocabulary.mnemonic: You open your 'mouth (口)' and say 'wéi' to get someone's attention, especially on the phone.
vocabulary.etymology: From the mouth (口) radical. Its use as a telephone greeting is influenced by the English 'hello.'

examples.pinyin: Wéi, nǐ hǎo, qǐng wèn Xiǎo Wáng zài ma?
examples.english: Hello, is Xiao Wang there?

examples.pinyin: Wéi! Xiǎoxīn chē!
examples.english: Hey! Watch out for the car!

vocabulary.usage_notes: 接电话的标准开头语。面对面喊人时语气可以比较直接。

vocabulary.mnemonic: You use your 'mouth (口)' and 'dare (敢)' to be loud and shout.
vocabulary.etymology: 口 (kǒu, mouth) radical + 敢 (gǎn, dare). To dare to open your mouth loudly.

examples.pinyin: Bié zài túshūguǎn hǎn.
examples.english: Don't shout in the library.

examples.pinyin: Māma zài lóuxià hǎn wǒ chī fàn.
examples.english: Mom is shouting for me to eat downstairs.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 声音比‘叫’更大、更用力，常带有情绪。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The part of your face that you 'zui' (think 'pursed lips') to kiss or talk.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally written as 觜 (zī, beak), later replaced by 嘴 with the 口 (mouth) radical to clarify its meaning.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiào de hé bù lǒng zuǐ.
examples.english: He was grinning from ear to ear.

examples.pinyin: Bì shàng zuǐ, tīng wǒ shuō.
examples.english: Shut your mouth and listen to me.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 口语中比‘口’更常用，指整个嘴巴（包括嘴唇）。

vocabulary.english: to return to one's home country
vocabulary.mnemonic: You 'return (回)' to your 'country (国).'
vocabulary.etymology: 回 (huí, to return) + 国 (guó, country).

examples.pinyin: Tā xià gè yuè jiù yào huí guó le.
examples.english: He is returning to his home country next month.

examples.pinyin: Huí guó hòu nǐ xiǎng zuò shénme?
examples.english: What do you want to do after returning home?

vocabulary.usage_notes: 特指回到自己的祖国。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Between 'countries (国)' and their 'borders (际)' — that's the international realm.
vocabulary.etymology: 国 (guó, country) + 际 (jì, border, between). Literally 'between nations.'

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè guójì wèntí.
examples.english: This is an international issue.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuān kàn guójì xīnwén.
examples.english: I like to watch international news.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常用作形容词，如‘国际机场’、‘国际学校’。

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'picture (图)' that is a flat 'slice (片)' of a scene.
vocabulary.etymology: 图 (tú, diagram, picture) + 片 (piàn, slice, sheet). A sheet bearing a picture.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng túpiàn pāi de zhēn hǎo.
examples.english: This picture was taken really well.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ túpiàn fā gěi wǒ.
examples.english: Please send me the picture.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 泛指各种图片，包括照片、插图、图表等。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'ground (地)' shaped like a 'ball (球)' we live on.
vocabulary.etymology: 地 (dì, earth, ground) + 球 (qiú, ball, sphere).

examples.pinyin: Dìqiú shì yuán de.
examples.english: The Earth is round.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen yào bǎohù dìqiú.
examples.english: We must protect the Earth.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 专有名词，通常要加‘the’。

vocabulary.mnemonic: An 'iron (铁)' train that runs 'underground (地).'
vocabulary.etymology: 地 (dì, ground, underground) + 铁 (tiě, iron, railroad).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měitiān zuò dìtiě shàngbān.
examples.english: I take the subway to work every day.

examples.pinyin: Shànghǎi de dìtiě hěn fāngbiàn.
examples.english: Shanghai's subway is very convenient.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 在中国城市常用。可以说‘坐地铁’、‘乘地铁’。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'station (站)' for the 'subway (地铁).'
vocabulary.etymology: 地铁 (dìtiě, subway) + 站 (zhàn, station).

examples.pinyin: Xià yī gè dìtiě zhàn xià chē.
examples.english: Get off at the next subway station.

examples.pinyin: Dìtiě zhàn lǐ rén hěn duō.
examples.english: There are a lot of people in the subway station.

vocabulary.english: field, site; (as MW) for events, games, etc.
vocabulary.mnemonic: An open 'field' or the site of an event.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted earth/ground (土) worked upon, evolving to mean an open space or arena.

examples.pinyin: Zúqiú chǎng zài nàlǐ.
examples.english: The soccer field is over there.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kànle yī chǎng diànyǐng.
examples.english: I watched a movie (a 'showing' of a film).

vocabulary.usage_notes: 作量词时读 chǎng，表示有始有终的事件，如一场雨、一场比赛。

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'person (人)' who is 'bad (坏).'
vocabulary.etymology: 坏 (huài, bad) + 人 (rén, person).

examples.chinese: 电影里的坏人最后被抓了。
examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng lǐ de huài rén zuìhòu bèi zhuā le.
examples.english: The villain in the movie was caught in the end.

examples.chinese: 不要相信陌生人，小心遇到坏人。
examples.pinyin: Bùyào xiāngxìn mòshēng rén, xiǎoxīn yùdào huài rén.
examples.english: Don't trust strangers; be careful of bad people.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常用于教育孩子或泛指道德低下的人。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'place (处)' where something is 'bad (坏)' — its drawbacks.
vocabulary.etymology: 坏 (huài, bad) + 处 (chù, place, aspect). The bad aspects.

examples.pinyin: Chōuyān yǒu hěn duō huàichu.
examples.english: Smoking has many disadvantages.

examples.pinyin: Zhèyàng zuò yǒu shénme huàichu?
examples.english: What's the downside of doing it this way?

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常与‘好处’对比使用。

vocabulary.mnemonic: A solid barrier, like the Great Wall, made of earth (土) and built strong.
vocabulary.etymology: Contains the radical 土 (tǔ, earth/soil), as many early walls were made of rammed earth.

examples.pinyin: Zhè miàn qiáng shì báisè de.
examples.english: This wall is white.

examples.pinyin: Bié zài qiáng shàng huà huà.
examples.english: Don't draw on the wall.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 指建筑物的墙壁，也用于比喻，如‘防火墙’。

vocabulary.mnemonic: What you 'hear (声)' and the 'tone (音)' it has.
vocabulary.etymology: 声 (shēng, sound) + 音 (yīn, tone, note). Combined they cover the concept of audible sound.

examples.chinese: 我听到一个奇怪的声音。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīngdào yī gè qíguài de shēngyīn.
examples.english: I heard a strange sound.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de shēngyīn zhēn hǎo tīng.
examples.english: Your voice is very pleasant.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 涵盖所有声音，包括人的嗓音、自然声、机器声等。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The season 'below (下)' the hot sun — think of the sun 'under' which it's hottest? Actually 夏 is the character for summer itself.
vocabulary.etymology: 夏 (xià, summer) + 天 (tiān, sky, day, season).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐhuān xiàtiān.
examples.english: I like summer the most.

examples.pinyin: Qùnián xiàtiān wǒ qù hǎibiān le.
examples.english: I went to the seaside last summer.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Food that is 'sold (卖)' for you to take 'out (外).'
vocabulary.etymology: 外 (wài, outside) + 卖 (mài, to sell).

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen jīn wǎn diǎn wàimài ba.
examples.english: Let's order takeout tonight.

examples.pinyin: Wàimài xiǎogē lái le.
examples.english: The delivery guy is here.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 可作名词‘一份外卖’，也可作动词‘外卖披萨’。

vocabulary.english: other parts of the country, out of town
vocabulary.mnemonic: A 'place (地)' that is 'outside (外)' your local area.
vocabulary.etymology: 外 (wài, outside) + 地 (dì, place).

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wàidì rén.
examples.english: He is from out of town.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīngcháng qù wàidì chūchāi.
examples.english: I often go to other cities on business trips.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 相对于说话人当前所在地而言。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Asking for 'many (多)' 'time units (久)'?
vocabulary.etymology: 多 (duō, many) + 久 (jiǔ, long time).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yào qù duō jiǔ?
examples.english: How long will you be gone?

examples.pinyin: Xué Zhōngwén xué le duō jiǔ le?
examples.english: How long have you been studying Chinese?

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用来询问时间长度，回答用‘三天’、‘一个小时’等。

vocabulary.mnemonic: Expresses degree: 'How (多)' 'indeed (么)'!
vocabulary.etymology: 多 (duō, many/much) + 么 (me, interrogative particle).

examples.pinyin: Duōme piàoliang de huā a!
examples.english: What beautiful flowers!

examples.pinyin: Tā duōme gāoxìng a!
examples.english: How happy he is!

vocabulary.usage_notes: 用于感叹句，强调程度高，常与‘啊’连用。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The sky has 'many (多) clouds (云).'
vocabulary.etymology: 多 (duō, many) + 云 (yún, cloud).

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān duōyún.
examples.english: It's cloudy today.

examples.pinyin: Míngtiān shì duōyún tiānqì.
examples.english: Tomorrow will be cloudy weather.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 天气预报常用词，介于‘晴’和‘阴/雨’之间。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'number (数)' that is 'many (多)' — the majority.
vocabulary.etymology: 多 (duō, many) + 数 (shù, number).

examples.pinyin: Duōshù rén dōu tóngyì le.
examples.english: Most people agreed.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen bān duōshù shì nǚshēng.
examples.english: The majority of our class are girls.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 常与‘少数’对比使用。

vocabulary.mnemonic: The time of darkness, the opposite of day.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictographic, possibly representing the moon and stars or a person resting under a cover at night.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gōngzuò dào shēnyè.
examples.english: I work late into the night.

examples.pinyin: Zuótiān xiàle yī yè de yǔ.
examples.english: It rained all night yesterday.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 书面感稍强，‘晚上’更口语化。常出现在固定搭配中，如‘夜里’、‘深夜’、‘一夜’等。

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 作 (does) work that makes them 家 (famous at home and abroad).
vocabulary.etymology: 作 (zuò, to do, to make) + 家 (jiā, home, specialist). Literally "one who makes (works) at home" or "specialist in creating."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie shì yī wèi zuòjiā.
examples.english: My older sister is a writer.

examples.pinyin: Nà wèi zuòjiā hěn shòu huānyíng.
examples.english: That author is very popular.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to someone who writes professionally, like novelists or essayists.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 作 (make) a 文 (written piece).
vocabulary.etymology: 作 (zuò, to do, to make) + 文 (wén, writing, language). Literally "made writing."

examples.chinese: 今天的作业是写一篇作文。
examples.pinyin: Jīntiān de zuòyè shì xiě yī piān zuòwén.
examples.english: Today's homework is to write an essay.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tǎoyàn xiě zuòwén.
examples.english: I hate writing compositions.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly refers to school essays or writing assignments.

vocabulary.english: effect, function, role (n); to act on (v)
vocabulary.mnemonic: What something 作 (does) and its 用 (use).
vocabulary.etymology: 作 (zuò, to do, to make) + 用 (yòng, to use). Literally "making use" or "use and effect."

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng yào yǒu shénme zuòyòng?
examples.english: What effect does this medicine have?

examples.pinyin: Tā zài gōngsī lǐ zuòyòng hěn dà.
examples.english: He plays a very important role in the company.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to describe the function or influence of something.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 使 (employ) it for its 用 (purpose).
vocabulary.etymology: 使 (shǐ, to cause, to employ) + 用 (yòng, to use).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ huì shǐyòng zhège ruǎnjiàn ma?
examples.english: Can you use this software?

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zhèngquè shǐyòng shèbèi.
examples.english: Please use the equipment correctly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal than just 用, but common in daily speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 列 (list) out 如 (as) an example.
vocabulary.etymology: 例 (lì, example) + 如 (rú, as, like). Literally "example as."

examples.chinese: 我喜欢运动，例如打篮球。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan yùndòng, lìrú dǎ lánqiú.
examples.english: I like sports, for example, playing basketball.

examples.chinese: 买些水果，例如苹果和香蕉。
examples.pinyin: Mǎi xiē shuǐguǒ, lìrú píngguǒ hé xiāngjiāo.
examples.english: Buy some fruit, such as apples and bananas.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to introduce an example. Often followed by a comma.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 例 (instance) 子 (itself).
vocabulary.etymology: 例 (lì, example) + 子 (zi, noun suffix).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gěi wǒ yī gè lìzi ma?
examples.english: Can you give me an example?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè hěn hǎo de lìzi.
examples.english: This is a very good example.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The concrete example itself, while 例如 is the phrase used to introduce it.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's 便 (convenient) for your 宜 (budget).
vocabulary.etymology: 便 (biàn, convenient, easy) + 宜 (yí, suitable, fitting). Originally meant "convenient and fitting," evolving to mean a favorable price.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yīfu hěn piányi.
examples.english: This piece of clothing is very cheap.

examples.chinese: 这里的水果便宜又新鲜。
examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shuǐguǒ piányi yòu xīnxiān.
examples.english: The fruit here is cheap and fresh.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Note the pronunciation is piányi, not biànyí in this meaning.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person 亻(人) says 言 words you can believe, sent in a letter.
vocabulary.etymology: From 人 (rén, person) + 言 (yán, speech). Original meaning related to sincerity and truth in speech, hence "to believe" and "a letter."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuótiān shōu dào yī fēng xìn.
examples.english: I received a letter yesterday.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xìn tā shuō de huà ma?
examples.english: Do you believe what he says?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Context determines if it's a noun (letter) or verb (believe).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 信 (message) giving a 号 (sign).
vocabulary.etymology: 信 (xìn, message, trust) + 号 (hào, sign, mark).

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ de shǒujī xìnhào bù hǎo.
examples.english: The cell phone signal here is bad.

examples.pinyin: Lǜdēng shì tōngxíng de xìnhào.
examples.english: A green light is the signal to go.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to any kind of signal: traffic, phone, Wi-Fi, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 信 (Believe) in your 心 (heart).
vocabulary.etymology: 信 (xìn, to believe) + 心 (xīn, heart, mind). Literally "believing heart."

examples.pinyin: Tā duì kǎoshì hěn yǒu xìnxīn.
examples.english: He is very confident about the exam.

examples.pinyin: Bié shīqù xìnxīn!
examples.english: Don't lose confidence!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common collocations: 有/没有信心 (have/lack confidence).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 信 (message) that 息 (rests) in data.
vocabulary.etymology: 信 (xìn, message) + 息 (xī, to rest, news). Historically, 息 also meant "news" or "intelligence."

examples.chinese: 我从网上找到了这个信息。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng wǎng shàng zhǎo dào le zhège xìnxī.
examples.english: I found this information online.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng cháshōu wǒ fā de xìnxī.
examples.english: Please check the message I sent.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common word for any kind of info or message (including texts).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 信用 (credit) 卡 (card).
vocabulary.etymology: 信用 (xìnyòng, credit) + 卡 (kǎ, card).

examples.chinese: 我可以用信用卡付款吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ kěyǐ yòng xìnyòngkǎ fùkuǎn ma?
examples.english: Can I pay with a credit card?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de xìnyòngkǎ diū le!
examples.english: I lost my credit card!

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person 亻(人) arrives 到 (to the ground) by falling.
vocabulary.etymology: Derived from 到 (dào, to arrive). The person radical (亻) was added to indicate a person's action of arriving... on the ground.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎoxīn, bié dǎo le!
examples.english: Be careful, don't fall down!

examples.pinyin: Nà kē shù bèi fēng chuī dǎo le.
examples.english: That tree was blown down by the wind.

vocabulary.usage_notes: This is the dǎo reading. Can also mean "to pour" when read as dào (different tone).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person 亻(人) who 昔 (in the past) took something and will return it.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (rén, person) + 昔 (xī, past). The idea is something that was someone else's in the past is temporarily with you.

examples.chinese: 我能借你的笔用一下吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ néng jiè nǐ de bǐ yòng yīxià ma?
examples.english: Can I borrow your pen for a moment?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiè gěi tā yībǎi kuài qián.
examples.english: I lent him one hundred yuan.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can mean both 'borrow' and 'lend.' Use 借给 to clearly mean 'lend to.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person 亻(人) is not truly 叚 (the real thing).
vocabulary.etymology: 亻 (rén, person) + 叚 (jiǎ, borrowed, not genuine). The original meaning is "not real."

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì jiǎ xīnwén.
examples.english: This is fake news.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen xià zhōu fàng sān tiān jià.
examples.english: We have a three-day holiday next week.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adjective, pronounced jiǎ (fake). As a noun for holiday, it's pronounced jià and is often part of the word 假期.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 假 (Holiday) 期 (period).
vocabulary.etymology: 假 (jià, holiday) + 期 (qī, period).

examples.chinese: 暑假假期你打算做什么？
examples.pinyin: Shǔjià jiàqī nǐ dǎsuàn zuò shénme?
examples.english: What do you plan to do during the summer vacation?

examples.pinyin: Zhège jiàqī guò de tài kuài le.
examples.english: This holiday passed too quickly.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the span of time, like summer break or a week off.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 作 (Do) it until you 到 (arrive at the goal).
vocabulary.etymology: 做 (zuò, to do) + 到 (dào, to arrive).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiāngxìn nǐ néng zuòdào.
examples.english: I believe you can do it.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhōngyú zuòdào le!
examples.english: He finally achieved it!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for achieving a specific task or goal.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 做 (doing) 法 (method).
vocabulary.etymology: 做 (zuò, to do) + 法 (fǎ, method, law).

examples.pinyin: Zhè dào cài de zuòfǎ hěn jiǎndān.
examples.english: The method for making this dish is very simple.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù xǐhuan tā de zuòfǎ.
examples.english: I don't like his way of doing things.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the method or approach to doing something.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 做 (Do) the 饭 (meal).
vocabulary.etymology: 做 (zuò, to do) + 饭 (fàn, meal, cooked rice).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ māma měitiān wǎnshàng zuòfàn.
examples.english: My mom cooks dinner every night.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng xué zuòfàn ma?
examples.english: Do you want to learn to cook?

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common verb for preparing a meal.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 亭 (Pavilion) is where people 停 (stop) to rest.
vocabulary.etymology: From 亭 (tíng, pavilion), a place where one stops. The 亻(人) radical was added to emphasize the human action of stopping.

examples.pinyin: Yǔ tíng le.
examples.english: The rain has stopped.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhèlǐ tíng yīxià chē.
examples.english: Please stop/park the car here for a moment.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for stopping movement, actions, or for parking vehicles.

vocabulary.english: to park a car, to stop a vehicle
vocabulary.mnemonic: 停 (Stop) the 车 (vehicle).
vocabulary.etymology: 停 (tíng, to stop) + 车 (chē, vehicle).

examples.pinyin: Zhèlǐ bùnéng tíngchē.
examples.english: You can't park here.

examples.pinyin: Zhǎo gè dìfang tíngchē ba.
examples.english: Let's find a place to park.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The general verb for parking a car or stopping a vehicle.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 停 (Parking) 车 (vehicle) 场 (field).
vocabulary.etymology: 停车 (tíngchē, to park) + 场 (chǎng, field, venue).

examples.chinese: 超市旁边有一个停车场。
examples.pinyin: Chāoshì pángbiān yǒu yī gè tíngchēchǎng.
examples.english: There is a parking lot next to the supermarket.

examples.pinyin: Tíngchēchǎng mǎn le.
examples.english: The parking lot is full.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A 健 (strong) person with a 康 (peaceful) life is healthy.
vocabulary.etymology: 健 (jiàn, strong, robust) + 康 (kāng, peaceful, prosperous). Together they convey robust well-being.

examples.chinese: 多吃蔬菜对身体很健康。
examples.pinyin: Duō chī shūcài duì shēntǐ hěn jiànkāng.
examples.english: Eating more vegetables is very healthy for your body.

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ shēntǐ jiànkāng!
examples.english: I wish you good health!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe a person, lifestyle, or refer to health as a concept.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A person 亻(人) who has a large 象 (elephant-like) similarity.
vocabulary.etymology: 亻 (rén, person) + 象 (xiàng, elephant, appearance). Originally meant "portrait" or "image," then evolved to mean "to resemble."

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zhǎng de xiàng nǐ māma.
examples.english: You look like your mother.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān xiàng chūntiān yīyàng nuǎnhuo.
examples.english: Today is warm like spring.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for comparing people or things. Often used with 一样 (yīyàng, the same).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Overcome 克 the tiny weight of a gram.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally meant "to overcome." Its use for the unit "gram" is a phonetic loan from the French "gramme."

examples.pinyin: Zhè dài táng yǒu wǔbǎi kè.
examples.english: This bag of sugar weighs five hundred grams.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le èrbǎi kè niúròu.
examples.english: I bought 200 grams of beef.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Standard unit of weight/mass. 1 公斤 (gōngjīn) = 1 kilogram = 1000克.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of entering (入) through the mouth (口) of a building.
vocabulary.etymology: 入 (enter) + 口 (mouth, opening). Literally "entering mouth."

examples.pinyin: Chāo shì de rù kǒu zài nà biān.
examples.english: The supermarket entrance is over there.

examples.pinyin: Dì tiě rù kǒu rén hěn duō.
examples.english: There are a lot of people at the subway entrance.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for physical entrances to places. Can be part of compound words like '入口处' (entrance area).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The king (王) under a roof (入-like shape) has it all.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a piece of flawless jade, later borrowed to mean "complete, whole."

examples.pinyin: Wǒ quán chī wán le.
examples.english: I ate it all up.

examples.pinyin: Tā quán tīng dǒng le.
examples.english: He understood all of it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can come before verbs (like '全懂了') or nouns (like '全中国'). A very common intensifier.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Whole (全) body (体) = the entire group of people.
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (whole) + 体 (body). Means "the whole body (of people)."

examples.pinyin: Quán tǐ tóng xué qǐng zhù yì!
examples.english: Attention, all students!

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì quán tǐ yuán gōng de yì jiàn.
examples.english: This is the opinion of all the staff.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Formal term for a collective group, often used in announcements or formal contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: All (全) of the country (国).
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (whole) + 国 (country, state).

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jié rì shì quán guó xìng de.
examples.english: This holiday is nationwide.

examples.pinyin: Tā zài quán guó dōu yǒu míng.
examples.english: He is famous all over the country.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Whole (全) family (家).
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (whole) + 家 (family, home).

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ men quán jiā xìng fú!
examples.english: Wishing happiness to your whole family!

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men quán jiā qù lǚ xíng le.
examples.english: Our whole family went on a trip.

vocabulary.mnemonic: All (全) year (年) long.
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (whole) + 年 (year).

examples.chinese: 这里的天气全年都很暖和。
examples.pinyin: Zhè lǐ de tiān qì quán nián dōu hěn nuǎn huo.
examples.english: The weather here is warm all year round.

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī yǒu quán nián de jì huà.
examples.english: The company has an annual plan.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Whole (全) body (身).
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (whole) + 身 (body).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ quán shēn dōu téng.
examples.english: My whole body aches.

examples.pinyin: Tā lèi de quán shēn méi lì qi.
examples.english: He's so tired that his whole body has no strength.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Whole (全) part/portion (部) = all the parts.
vocabulary.etymology: 全 (whole) + 部 (part, section).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de zuò yè quán bù zuò wán le.
examples.english: I've finished all of my homework.

examples.pinyin: Qián quán bù dōu huā guāng le.
examples.english: All the money has been spent.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often interchangeable with 全 but sounds slightly more formal/comprehensive.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) transport (交) vehicle (车).
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public) + 交 (traffic, transport) + 车 (vehicle).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi tiān zuò gōng jiāo chē shàng bān.
examples.english: I take the bus to work every day.

examples.chinese: 下一辆公交车什么时候来？
examples.pinyin: Xià yī liàng gōng jiāo chē shén me shí hou lái?
examples.english: When is the next bus coming?

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common word for 'bus' in spoken Mandarin. Slightly shorter/casual version of 公共汽车.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公共) steam/vehicle (汽车). A bit more formal name for the bus.
vocabulary.etymology: 公共 (public) + 汽车 (automobile, car). Literally "public automobile."

examples.pinyin: Gōng gòng qì chē shàng rén tài duō le.
examples.english: There are too many people on the bus.

examples.pinyin: Zuò gōng gòng qì chē pián yi yī diǎn.
examples.english: Taking the bus is a bit cheaper.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Synonymous with 公交车. It's the full, formal term, but also perfectly common in speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) management (司). Where business is managed.
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public) + 司 (manage, take charge).

examples.chinese: 我在一家科技公司工作。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài yī jiā kē jì gōng sī gōng zuò.
examples.english: I work at a tech company.

examples.chinese: 我们公司下个月要搬家。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men gōng sī xià ge yuè yào bān jiā.
examples.english: Our company is moving to a new office next month.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard word for any incorporated business or firm.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) garden (园).
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public) + 园 (garden, park).

examples.chinese: 周末我们去公园野餐吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò wǒ men qù gōng yuán yě cān ba.
examples.english: Let's go have a picnic in the park this weekend.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge gōng yuán tè bié dà.
examples.english: This park is especially big.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) level/even (平) treatment.
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public, impartial) + 平 (level, even).

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jué dìng hěn gōng píng.
examples.english: This decision is very fair.

examples.chinese: 老师对我们每个人都很公平。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo shī duì wǒ men měi ge rén dōu hěn gōng píng.
examples.english: The teacher is fair to every one of us.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes situations, rules, people, etc. that are just and unbiased.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) weight unit (斤). The metric 'public' version of the traditional Chinese catty (斤).
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public, metric) + 斤 (catty, a traditional Chinese unit of weight).

examples.pinyin: Píng guǒ duō shǎo qián yī gōng jīn?
examples.english: How much is one kilogram of apples?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mǎi le sān gōng jīn dà mǐ.
examples.english: I bought three kilograms of rice.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard metric unit for weight in daily life. Synonymous with 千克 (qiān kè).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) road (路).
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public) + 路 (road, path).

examples.pinyin: Yán zhe zhè tiáo gōng lù yī zhí kāi.
examples.english: Drive straight along this highway.

examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò gōng lù shàng de chē hěn duō.
examples.english: There are a lot of cars on the highway on weekends.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to public roads, especially intercity or open roads, not small streets.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Public (公) unit of distance (里). The metric version of the traditional Chinese li (里).
vocabulary.etymology: 公 (public, metric) + 里 (li, a traditional Chinese unit of distance).

examples.chinese: 从我家到公司有五公里。
examples.pinyin: Cóng wǒ jiā dào gōng sī yǒu wǔ gōng lǐ.
examples.english: It's five kilometers from my home to the company.

examples.pinyin: Tā měi tiān pǎo sān gōng lǐ.
examples.english: He runs three kilometers every day.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The standard unit for long distances in daily life. Synonymous with 千米 (qiān mǐ).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Close the gate (关) on your heart (心) to protect it? Actually, it's to be concerned about what's inside your heart.
vocabulary.etymology: 关 (to close, to involve) + 心 (heart). Originally meant to be anxious/worried, now means to care/be concerned.

examples.pinyin: Xiè xie nǐ zhè me guān xīn wǒ.
examples.english: Thank you for caring about me so much.

examples.chinese: 妈妈总是关心我的健康。
examples.pinyin: Mā ma zǒng shì guān xīn wǒ de jiàn kāng.
examples.english: My mom always cares about my health.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Expresses emotional concern for someone's wellbeing. Object is usually a person or abstract thing (健康, 学习).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Close (关) the machine (机).
vocabulary.etymology: 关 (to close, shut off) + 机 (machine, device).

examples.pinyin: Shuì jiào qián jì de guān jī.
examples.english: Remember to turn off (the device) before sleeping.

examples.chinese: 我手机快没电了，要关机了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǒu jī kuài méi diàn le, yào guān jī le.
examples.english: My phone is almost out of battery, I have to turn it off.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specific to electronic devices like phones, computers, TVs. 关灯 is for lights.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Its (其) middle (中). Inside the group.
vocabulary.etymology: 其 (its, that) + 中 (middle, inside).

examples.chinese: 我有三个朋友，其中两个是医生。
