examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu sān ge péng you, qí zhōng liǎng ge shì yī shēng.
examples.english: I have three friends, two of whom are doctors.

examples.chinese: 他有很多爱好，读书是其中之一。
examples.pinyin: Tā yǒu hěn duō ài hào, dú shū shì qí zhōng zhī yī.
examples.english: He has many hobbies, reading is one of them.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to specify a subset within a larger group mentioned just before. Often paired with 是.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Its (其) different/other (他).
vocabulary.etymology: 其 (its, that) + 他 (other). 他 originally meant 'other' before specializing to 'he/him.'

examples.chinese: 我只认识他，不认识其他人。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhǐ rèn shi tā, bú rèn shi qí tā rén.
examples.english: I only know him, I don't know the other people.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ hái yǒu qí tā wèn tí ma?
examples.english: Do you have any other questions?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common. Used for non-specific others. 别的 (bié de) is more casual and often interchangeable.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Shepherd (⺶) with food (食) raises animals.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 養. The top part (⺶) relates to sheep/herding, the bottom (食) is food. The idea is to provide food for raising.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā yǎng le yī zhī xiǎo māo.
examples.english: My family keeps/raises a little cat.

examples.pinyin: Tā yī ge rén yǎng huó le quán jiā.
examples.english: He alone supported/raised the whole family.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for raising pets (养狗), children (养孩子), plants (养花), or supporting a family (养家).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The season (天) that feels like being stuck (冬 - depicts hanging icicles).
vocabulary.etymology: 冬 (winter) + 天 (season, day, heaven).

examples.pinyin: Běi jīng de dōng tiān fēi cháng lěng.
examples.english: Winter in Beijing is very cold.

examples.chinese: 我最喜欢的季节是冬天。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐ huan de jì jié shì dōng tiān.
examples.english: My favorite season is winter.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Follow the standard (准) and be sure/correct (确).
vocabulary.etymology: 准 (allow, standard) + 确 (true, sure).

examples.pinyin: Tā de fā yīn hěn zhǔn què.
examples.english: His pronunciation is very accurate.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge dá àn bù zhǔn què.
examples.english: This answer is not accurate.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for descriptions, measurements, translations, etc. that are precise and correct.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Ice (冫) in the capital (京)? Feels cool.
vocabulary.etymology: 冫 (ice radical) + 京 (capital). The ice radical indicates coldness.

examples.pinyin: Wǎn shang tiān qì yǒu diǎn liáng.
examples.english: The weather is a bit cool in the evening.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bēi shuǐ tài liáng le.
examples.english: This glass of water is too cool/cold.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes a pleasantly low temperature, not freezing cold (冷). Often used for weather, drinks, or objects.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Cool (凉) and quick/refreshing (快) feeling.
vocabulary.etymology: 凉 (cool) + 快 (fast, quickly; here meaning refreshing).

examples.pinyin: Shù dǐ xia zhēn liáng kuai.
examples.english: It's really nice and cool under the tree.

examples.pinyin: Zán men jìn wū liáng kuai liáng kuai ba.
examples.english: Let's go inside to cool off.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A positive, pleasant kind of coolness. Can be reduplicated as a verb (凉快凉快) meaning 'to cool off.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: The horror movie was SO 可怕, it made you say '可(kě)' [oh] '怕(pà)' [afraid]!
vocabulary.etymology: 可 originally meant 'to approve,' but here it functions as an intensifier. 怕 means 'to fear.' Together they intensify fear.

examples.pinyin: Nà ge shēng yīn tài kě pà le.
examples.english: That sound is too scary.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuò le ge kě pà de mèng.
examples.english: I had a terrifying dream.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to describe things, situations, or people that cause fear.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You agree '可(kě)' [yes], then change your mind with '是(shì)' [it is...] BUT...
vocabulary.etymology: 可 means 'may, can, approve.' 是 means 'to be.' Historically, it functioned to introduce a contrasting clause.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng qù, kě shì wǒ méi shí jiān.
examples.english: I want to go, but I don't have time.

examples.pinyin: Tā hěn lèi, kě shì hái zài gōng zuò.
examples.english: He is very tired, but he's still working.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in the middle of a sentence to introduce a contrast. Similar to 但是 but slightly softer.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You see it and say '可(kě)' [oh], I '爱(ài)' [love] it! It's so CUTE!
vocabulary.etymology: 可 (intensifier) + 爱 (to love). Literally 'worthy of love' or 'lovable.'

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī xiǎo māo zhēn kě ài!
examples.english: This little kitten is so cute!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de bǎo bao tài kě ài le.
examples.english: Your baby is too adorable.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for people, animals, or things that are endearing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Is it 可(kě) [can]? Is it 能(néng) [able]? It's POSSIBLE!
vocabulary.etymology: 可 (can, may) + 能 (ability, can). Together they reinforce the idea of potential or possibility.

examples.pinyin: Tā kě néng míng tiān lái.
examples.english: He might come tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì bù kě néng de shì.
examples.english: This is an impossible thing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used before a verb (可能来) or at the start of a sentence (可能吧).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The one who 司(sī) [manages] the 机(jī) [machine] is the DRIVER.
vocabulary.etymology: 司 means 'to take charge of, manage.' 机 is short for 机器 (machine), referring to the vehicle.

examples.pinyin: Chū zū chē sī jī zhī dào lù.
examples.english: The taxi driver knows the way.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bà ba shì gōng jiāo chē sī jī.
examples.english: My dad is a bus driver.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for professional drivers (taxi, bus, truck). For someone driving casually, use 开车的人.

vocabulary.mnemonic: This 合(hé) [fits together] with the 适(shì) [right] situation. It's SUITABLE.
vocabulary.etymology: 合 means 'to combine, fit.' 适 means 'to fit, to suit.' Together they emphasize appropriateness.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiàn yī fu nǐ chuān hěn hé shì.
examples.english: This piece of clothing looks very fitting on you.

examples.pinyin: Xiàn zài bú shì hé shì de shí jiān.
examples.english: Now is not a suitable time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe things, times, or people that are appropriate for a specific purpose.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 你们一起 同(tóng) [same] 事(shì) [work/business]. You are COWORKERS.
vocabulary.etymology: 同 (same, together) + 事 (matter, work, business). Refers to people who share the same work.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hé tóng shì yī qǐ chī wǔ fàn.
examples.english: I eat lunch with my colleagues.

examples.pinyin: Tā shì wǒ de xīn tóng shì.
examples.english: She is my new coworker.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers specifically to people you work with, not just friends.

vocabulary.mnemonic: When two things happen at the 同(tóng) [same] 时(shí) [time].
vocabulary.etymology: 同 (same) + 时 (time). Literally 'same time.'

examples.chinese: 他一边听音乐，同时在做作业。
examples.pinyin: Tā yī biān tīng yīn yuè, tóng shí zài zuò zuò yè.
examples.english: He listens to music while doing homework.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men tóng shí dào dá.
examples.english: We arrived at the same time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with 一边...一边... or to connect two parallel actions or facts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 有 同(tóng) [same] 样(yàng) [appearance/kind]. They look the SAME.
vocabulary.etymology: 同 (same) + 样 (appearance, manner). Literally 'same appearance/sort.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng yào tóng yàng de kā fēi.
examples.english: I want the same coffee.

examples.pinyin: Tā tóng yàng xǐ huan kàn diàn yǐng.
examples.english: He also likes watching movies.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as an adjective (同样的) or adverb (同样地/同样).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The evening (夕) moon (月) lights up your NAME.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of a mouth (口) calling out in the evening (夕), indicating 'to name' or 'a name.'

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiào shén me míng?
examples.english: What's your name?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men bān yǒu sān shí míng xué shēng.
examples.english: There are thirty students in our class.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In casual speech, 名字 is more common for 'name.' As a measure word, it's formal for people (e.g., 一名医生).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一张写着大家 名(míng) [names] 单(dān) [sheet] 的纸。A NAME LIST.
vocabulary.etymology: 名 (name) + 单 (list, bill, sheet).

examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài míng dān shang qiān míng.
examples.english: Please sign your name on the list.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì kè rén míng dān.
examples.english: This is the guest list.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for any list of names (e.g., attendees, employees, winners).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 事物的正式 名(míng) [name] 称(chēng) [called] what? It's the official TITLE.
vocabulary.etymology: 名 (name) + 称 (to call, name).

examples.chinese: 这个产品的名称是什么？
examples.pinyin: Zhè ge chǎn pǐn de míng chēng shì shén me?
examples.english: What is the name of this product?

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī de quán chēng hěn cháng.
examples.english: The company's full title is very long.

vocabulary.usage_notes: More formal than 名字. Often used for official names of organizations, products, or technical terms.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 事情发生 后(hòu) [after] 来(lái) [comes] what? AFTERWARDS.
vocabulary.etymology: 后 (after, behind) + 来 (to come). Literally 'after coming.'

examples.chinese: 他先走了，后来我也走了。
examples.pinyin: Tā xiān zǒu le, hòu lái wǒ yě zǒu le.
examples.english: He left first, and later I left too.

examples.pinyin: Hòu lái fā shēng le shén me?
examples.english: What happened afterwards?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to narrate past events in sequence. Differs from 以后 (which can be future).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The person under the roof (宀) turns their mouth (口) TOWARD something.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of a person facing a specific direction. Originally meant 'window,' then 'direction.'

examples.pinyin: Xiàng zuǒ zǒu.
examples.english: Walk toward the left.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiàng lǎo shī wèn hǎo.
examples.english: He greeted the teacher.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a preposition, indicates direction (向 + place/direction + verb). Also used in 向...学习/问好.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 听(tīng) [listen] to someone 讲(jiǎng) [speak/lecture].
vocabulary.etymology: 听 (to listen) + 讲 (to speak, to lecture).

examples.pinyin: Shàng kè yào rèn zhēn tīng jiǎng.
examples.english: You must listen to the lecture attentively in class.

examples.pinyin: Tā tīng jiǎng de shí hou jì bǐ jì.
examples.english: He takes notes while listening to the lecture.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to listening to a formal talk, lecture, or teaching. More formal than just 听.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 你 听(tīng) [hear] 说(shuō) [someone say] something. You HEAR ABOUT it.
vocabulary.etymology: 听 (to listen) + 说 (to say). Literally 'listen and say,' implying hearing something from others.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ tīng shuō tā yào bān jiā le.
examples.english: I heard he's going to move.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ tīng shuō le ma?
examples.english: Have you heard about it?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used when the information source is indirect (someone told you, or it's general hearsay).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The mouth (口) 吹 air like the wind.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictophonetic: 口 (mouth) suggests meaning, 欠 (to lack, yawn) suggests sound/action. Originally depicted blowing with the mouth.

examples.pinyin: Wài miàn zài chuī dà fēng.
examples.english: It's blowing hard outside.

examples.pinyin: Bāng wǒ bǎ là zhú chuī miè.
examples.english: Help me blow out the candle.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to wind blowing, or a person blowing on something (candle, hot food). Also slang for boasting (吹牛).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A field (田) with mouths (口) all around marks a complete CYCLE or WEEK.
vocabulary.etymology: Ancient pictograph of a field with crops planted all around, indicating completeness or a cycle.

examples.pinyin: Yì zhōu yǒu qī tiān.
examples.english: There are seven days in a week.

examples.pinyin: Tā xìng Zhōu.
examples.english: His surname is Zhou.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a measure word for weeks, often used in 一周/两周. For 'week' as a concept, 星期 is more common in casual speech.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 周(zhōu) [cycle] 年(nián) [year] later. It's the ANNIVERSARY.
vocabulary.etymology: 周 (cycle, complete round) + 年 (year). A full cycle of a year.

examples.chinese: 明天是他们的结婚周年。
examples.pinyin: Míng tiān shì tā men de jié hūn zhōu nián.
examples.english: Tomorrow is their wedding anniversary.

examples.pinyin: Gōng sī chéng lì shí zhōu nián.
examples.english: The company's 10th anniversary.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in compounds like 结婚周年, 周年纪念日.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 一 周(zhōu) [week] 末(mò) [end]. The WEEKEND!
vocabulary.etymology: 周 (week) + 末 (end, tip). The end of the week.

examples.pinyin: Zhōu mò nǐ dǎ suàn zuò shén me?
examples.english: What are you planning to do this weekend?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zhōu mò qù pá shān ba.
examples.english: Let's go hiking this weekend.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In mainland China, typically refers to Saturday and Sunday.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 味(wèi) [taste] and 道(dào) [way] of the food. Its FLAVOR.
vocabulary.etymology: 味 (taste, smell) + 道 (path, way, principle). The 'way' or characteristic of a taste/smell.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge cài de wèi dao bú cuò.
examples.english: This dish tastes good.

examples.pinyin: Shén me wèi dao? Hǎo xiāng a!
examples.english: What's that smell? So fragrant!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to both taste and smell. In speech, 'dao' is often neutral tone (wèi dao).

vocabulary.mnemonic: I'm telling you, 咱(zá) means YOU AND ME together.
vocabulary.etymology: Fusion of 自 (self) and 俺 (I, me - dialectal). Evolved to mean inclusive 'we.'

examples.pinyin: Zá qù nǎr chī fàn?
examples.english: Where shall we go to eat?

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì zá de jiā.
examples.english: This is our home.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Informal, common in northern dialects. Always includes the listener. Singular 'I/me' usage is dialectal.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 咱(zán) 们(men) [plural suffix] - a group that includes YOU.
vocabulary.etymology: 咱 (inclusive we) + 们 (plural suffix for pronouns).

examples.pinyin: Zán men zǒu ba!
examples.english: Let's go!

examples.pinyin: Zán men shì hǎo péng you.
examples.english: We are good friends.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Standard Mandarin for inclusive 'we' (you + me + possibly others). 我们 can be inclusive or exclusive.

vocabulary.english: loud, noisy; to make a sound
vocabulary.mnemonic: Someone speaking (口) in the direction (向) of you makes a LOUD sound.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictophonetic: 口 (mouth) suggests meaning, 向 (direction) suggests sound. Originally meant 'echo.'

examples.pinyin: Yīn yuè tài xiǎng le.
examples.english: The music is too loud.

examples.pinyin: Diàn huà xiǎng le.
examples.english: The phone rang.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adjective: loud. As a verb: to ring, to sound, to make a noise.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Two eyes (目) with a drop of water (丶) and a big mouth (口) - the picture of CRYING.
vocabulary.etymology: Ancient pictograph of a person with eyes (目) and a mouth (口) open, with a tear (丶).

examples.pinyin: Bié kū le, méi shì de.
examples.english: Don't cry, it's okay.

examples.pinyin: Hái zi kū de hěn lì hai.
examples.english: The child is crying very hard.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used for shedding tears (weep) or making crying sounds (wail).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 人 (rén) = person, 们 (men) = plural marker. It's the 'people-m' (men).
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (rén) depicts a person. 们 (men) is a modern grammatical suffix indicating plurality.

examples.chinese: 人们都喜欢去公园散步。
examples.pinyin: Rén men dōu xǐ huān qù gōng yuán sàn bù.
examples.english: People all like to go for walks in the park.

examples.chinese: 一到周末，这里的人们就特别多。
examples.pinyin: Yī dào zhōu mò, zhè lǐ de rén men jiù tè bié duō.
examples.english: As soon as the weekend comes, the people here are especially many.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A general term for a group of people, not necessarily specific individuals.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 人 (people) + 口 (mouth) = how many mouths to feed = population.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (rén) = person. 口 (kǒu) = mouth, opening. Historically used to count households by 'mouths'.

examples.chinese: 这个城市的人口超过一千万。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè chéng shì de rén kǒu chāo guò yī qiān wàn.
examples.english: This city's population is over ten million.

examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó shì rén kǒu dà guó.
examples.english: China is a country with a large population.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the total number of people in a specific area.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 人 (people) + 数 (number) = person-number.
vocabulary.etymology: 人 (rén) = person. 数 (shù) = number, to count.

examples.pinyin: Cān jiā huì yì de rén shù bù duō.
examples.english: The number of people attending the meeting isn't large.

examples.chinese: 你们班的学生人数是多少？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ men bān de xué sheng rén shù shì duō shao?
examples.english: What's the number of students in your class?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically refers to a counted headcount of people.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of it as a 'Yi' (亿) that's a HUGE number, like 100 million.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified 亿 combines 人 (person, phonetic) and 乙 (second, possibly meaning 'great number'). Traditional 億 is phonetic (意 yì) with radical 人 (person).

examples.pinyin: Zhōng guó yǒu shí sì yì duō rén kǒu.
examples.english: China has a population of over 1.4 billion.

examples.chinese: 这个视频有上亿的播放量。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè shì pín yǒu shàng yì de bō fàng liàng.
examples.english: This video has hundreds of millions of plays.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A unit of 100,000,000 (10^8). Crucial for talking about large-scale Chinese figures.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 什么 (what) + 样 (appearance/kind) = what-kind-of.
vocabulary.etymology: 什么 (shén me) = what. 样 (yàng) = appearance, kind, pattern.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎng yào shén me yàng de shǒu jī?
examples.english: What kind of phone do you want?

examples.pinyin: Tā shì shén me yàng de rén?
examples.english: What kind of person is he?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to ask about the nature, type, or quality of something. Followed by 的 (de).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 今 (now) + 后 (after) = the 'after-now' time.
vocabulary.etymology: 今 (jīn) = now, present. 后 (hòu) = after, behind.

examples.chinese: 今后我要好好学习中文。
examples.pinyin: Jīn hòu wǒ yào hǎo hǎo xué xí Zhōng wén.
examples.english: From now on, I will study Chinese well.

examples.pinyin: Xī wàng nǐ jīn hòu yī qiè shùn lì.
examples.english: I hope everything goes smoothly for you from now on.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Emphasizes the starting point as 'now' and looks forward.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 从 (from) + 小 (small) = from being small/young.
vocabulary.etymology: 从 (cóng) = from, follow. 小 (xiǎo) = small, young.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ cóng xiǎo jiù bù ài chī shū cài.
examples.english: I haven't liked eating vegetables since I was little.

examples.pinyin: Tā cóng xiǎo zài Běi jīng zhǎng dà.
examples.english: He grew up in Beijing since childhood.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe habits or situations that began in early life.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 以 (with) + 上 (up) = up-with, meaning 'and above'.
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (yǐ) = with, by means of. 上 (shàng) = up, above.

examples.chinese: 三岁以上的孩子可以参加。
examples.pinyin: Sān suì yǐ shàng de hái zi kě yǐ cān jiā.
examples.english: Children aged three and above can participate.

examples.pinyin: Yuè shōu rù yī wàn yuán yǐ shàng.
examples.english: Monthly income of more than ten thousand yuan.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Placed after a number/standard to mean 'that number or higher'. The opposite of 以下.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 以 (with) + 下 (down) = down-with, meaning 'and below'.
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (yǐ) = with, by means of. 下 (xià) = down, below.

examples.pinyin: Jià gé zài yī bǎi yuán yǐ xià.
examples.english: The price is below 100 yuan.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng yuè dú yǐ xià nèi róng.
examples.english: Please read the following content.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Placed after a number to mean 'that number or lower'. Can also mean 'the following' (as in text).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 以 (take) + 为 (as) = 'take as'... but you're often wrong.
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (yǐ) = take, use. 为 (wéi) = act as, be.

examples.chinese: 我以为今天是星期六呢！
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐ wéi jīn tiān shì xīng qī liù ne!
examples.english: I thought today was Saturday! (but it's not)

examples.pinyin: Bié yǐ wéi wǒ bù zhī dào.
examples.english: Don't assume I don't know.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Most often used when your assumption turns out to be incorrect. Often followed by 原来... (but actually...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 以 (with) + 前 (front) = the time in front of now (the past is ahead in Chinese spatial metaphor).
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (yǐ) = with, by. 前 (qián) = front, forward.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐ qián zhù zài Shàng hǎi.
examples.english: I lived in Shanghai before.

examples.pinyin: Sān tiān yǐ qián wǒ men jiàn guo miàn.
examples.english: We met three days ago.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a time period before a reference point (often the present). Can follow time words.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 以 (with) + 后 (behind) = the time behind now (the future is behind in Chinese spatial metaphor).
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (yǐ) = with, by. 后 (hòu) = behind, after.

examples.chinese: 吃完饭以后我们去散步吧。
examples.pinyin: Chī wán fàn yǐ hòu wǒ men qù sàn bù ba.
examples.english: After we finish eating, let's go for a walk.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǐ hòu xiǎng dāng yī shēng.
examples.english: I want to be a doctor in the future.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a time period after a reference point (an event or the present).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 以 (with) + 外 (outside) = the outside-with area.
vocabulary.etymology: 以 (yǐ) = with, by. 外 (wài) = outside.

examples.chinese: 除了工作以外，他没什么爱好。
examples.pinyin: Chú le gōng zuò yǐ wài, tā méi shén me ài hào.
examples.english: Apart from work, he doesn't have any hobbies.

examples.chinese: 学校以外的地方不能抽烟。
examples.pinyin: Xué xiào yǐ wài de dì fang bù néng chōu yān.
examples.english: You cannot smoke in places outside the school.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with 除了 (chú le) to mean 'except for, besides'. Marks exclusion.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It measures 'things' like shirts and matters. Think of a clothes hanger for a 件 (jiàn) shirt.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a person (亻) splitting something (牛). Evolved to mean 'item, piece'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīn tiān mǎi le liǎng jiàn T xù.
examples.english: I bought two T-shirts today.

examples.pinyin: Yǒu jiàn shì xiǎng gēn nǐ shāng liang.
examples.english: There's a matter I'd like to discuss with you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common measure word for clothing, matters, luggage, gifts, etc. Also used as a noun for 'matter' or 'item'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of cutting a cake into 份 (fèn) portions.
vocabulary.etymology: From 分 (fēn, to divide) with radical 亻 (person), emphasizing a person's share.

examples.pinyin: Gěi wǒ lái yī fèn chǎo fàn.
examples.english: Give me one portion of fried rice.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ de nà fèn.
examples.english: This is my share.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Measures portions of food, shares, copies of documents, jobs, feelings, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 休 (rest) + 假 (leave/holiday) = rest-leave.
vocabulary.etymology: 休 (xiū) = to rest (person 亻 leaning against a tree 木). 假 (jià) = holiday, leave.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xià gè yuè yào xiū jià yī zhōu.
examples.english: I'm going to take a week off next month.

examples.pinyin: Tā zhèng zài guó wài xiū jià.
examples.english: He is on vacation abroad right now.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to taking formal leave from work or study. Object is usually a time period.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's a short and sharp 'but' — 但 (dàn).
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 但. Original form meant 'bare, naked', later borrowed for its sound to mean 'only, but'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hěn xiǎng qù, dàn méi yǒu shí jiān.
examples.english: I really want to go, but I don't have time.

examples.chinese: 东西很便宜，但质量很好。
examples.pinyin: Dōng xi hěn pián yi, dàn zhì liàng hěn hǎo.
examples.english: The stuff is cheap, but the quality is good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A slightly more formal/written equivalent of 但是. Often used in the middle of a sentence.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of giving someone a seat (位 wèi) out of respect.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts a person 亻 standing in a place 立. Means 'position, seat', extended to a respectful counter for people.

measure_word.example: 三位老师 (sān wèi lǎo shī) - three teachers

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi shì wǒ de péng you.
examples.english: This (person) is my friend.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng wèn nín jǐ wèi?
examples.english: Excuse me, how many people (in your party)?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A polite measure word for people (especially guests, customers, elders). Not used for oneself or children.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The radical is 亻(person), with 氐(dǐ, base) below — a person low to the ground.
vocabulary.etymology: From 人 (person) + 氐 (dǐ, foundation, low). Means 'low, to lower'.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān de wēn dù hěn dī.
examples.english: Today's temperature is very low.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng nǐ bǎ shēng yīn fàng dī yī diǎn.
examples.english: Please lower your voice a bit.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Opposite of 高 (gāo). Can describe height, level, volume, price, status, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 住 (live) + 房 (house) = live-house.
vocabulary.etymology: 住 (zhù) = to live, reside. 房 (fáng) = house, room.

examples.chinese: 城市的住房问题很严重。
examples.pinyin: Chéng shì de zhù fáng wèn tí hěn yán zhòng.
examples.english: The city's housing problem is very serious.

examples.pinyin: Tā men gǎi shàn le zhù fáng tiáo jiàn.
examples.english: They improved their housing conditions.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to housing as a general concept or living space, often in formal/social contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 住 (stay) + 院 (courtyard/institution) = stay in the hospital courtyard.
vocabulary.etymology: 住 (zhù) = to stay, reside. 院 (yuàn) = courtyard, compound (e.g., hospital 医院).

examples.pinyin: Tā shēng bìng le, xū yào zhù yuàn.
examples.english: He's sick and needs to be hospitalized.

examples.chinese: 我爷爷住院一个星期了。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ yé ye zhù yuàn yī gè xīng qī le.
examples.english: My grandpa has been in the hospital for a week.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A separable verb (V-O). You can say 住过院 (have been hospitalized) or 住三天院 (be hospitalized for three days).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 体 (body) + 育 (nurture) = nurture the body.
vocabulary.etymology: 体 (tǐ) = body. 育 (yù) = to nurture, rear, educate.

examples.chinese: 我最喜欢的课是体育课。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐ huān de kè shì tǐ yù kè.
examples.english: My favorite class is P.E.

examples.pinyin: Tā tǐ yù tè bié hǎo.
examples.english: He's really good at sports.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The general term for sports and physical education. Often used in compounds.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 体育 (sports) + 场 (field) = sports-field.
vocabulary.etymology: 体育 (tǐ yù) = sports. 场 (chǎng) = field, ground, venue.

measure_word.example: 一个体育场 (yī gè tǐ yù chǎng) - a stadium

examples.chinese: 我们去体育场看足球比赛吧。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men qù tǐ yù chǎng kàn zú qiú bǐ sài ba.
examples.english: Let's go to the stadium to watch a soccer match.

examples.chinese: 这个体育场能坐五万人。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè tǐ yù chǎng néng zuò wǔ wàn rén.
examples.english: This stadium can seat fifty thousand people.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually refers to a large outdoor stadium for watching sports events.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 体育 (sports) + 馆 (building) = sports-building.
vocabulary.etymology: 体育 (tǐ yù) = sports. 馆 (guǎn) = building, hall (for public use).

measure_word.example: 一个体育馆 (yī gè tǐ yù guǎn) - a gymnasium

examples.chinese: 学校体育馆里有篮球场。
examples.pinyin: Xué xiào tǐ yù guǎn li yǒu lán qiú chǎng.
examples.english: There's a basketball court in the school gym.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ měi zhōu qù tǐ yù guǎn sān cì.
examples.english: I go to the gym three times a week.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually refers to an indoor facility for sports and exercise, often multi-purpose.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 作 (do) + 业 (work/task) = do-work.
vocabulary.etymology: 作 (zuò) = to do, make. 业 (yè) = work, business, task.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hái méi xiě zuò yè ne.
examples.english: I haven't done my homework yet.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān de zuò yè tài duō le!
examples.english: Today's homework is way too much!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Most common meaning is school homework. Can also refer to a work assignment or operation in other contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 拿 (hold) + 出 (out) = physically take something out, like from a pocket or bag.
vocabulary.etymology: Verb-Resultative Compound. 拿 (ná) means 'to hold' or 'to take,' and 出 (chū) means 'out.' Combined, they form a directional verb meaning 'to take out.'

examples.pinyin: Qǐng ná chū nǐ de shēn fèn zhèng.
examples.english: Please take out your ID card.

examples.chinese: 他从书包里拿出一本书。
examples.pinyin: Tā cóng shū bāo lǐ ná chū yī běn shū.
examples.english: He took a book out of his backpack.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used when you need to physically produce something.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You reach out (拿) and it arrives (到) in your hand. Think of 'getting your hands on something.'
vocabulary.etymology: Verb-Resultative Compound. 拿 (ná) is 'to take,' and 到 (dào) indicates successful completion or arrival. Means 'to have successfully taken/gotten.'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ ná dào jià zhào le!
examples.english: I got my driver's license!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ ná dào nà fèn wén jiàn le ma?
examples.english: Did you get that document?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies success in obtaining something you aimed for.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It stands TALL (挺 as in 挺直) above average, so it's 'quite' good.
vocabulary.etymology: The character 挺 originally meant 'straight' or 'upright' (from 扌 hand radical and 廷 courtyard). The sense of 'quite' or 'rather' is an adverbial extension implying something stands out positively.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng tǐng hǎo kàn de.
examples.english: This movie is pretty good.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān tiān qì tǐng hǎo.
examples.english: The weather is quite nice today.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common, slightly informal intensifier. Often softer than 很.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 挺 (quite) + 好 (good) = sounds like 'ting hao' -> 'tingle-good!'
vocabulary.etymology: A common phrase combining the intensifier 挺 (tǐng) with the adjective 好 (hǎo).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ de zhōng wén tǐng hǎo!
examples.english: Your Chinese is pretty good!

examples.pinyin: Zhè yàng ān pái tǐng hǎo.
examples.english: This arrangement is quite good.

vocabulary.usage_notes: An extremely common, positive, and casual expression of approval.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 扌 (hand) + 奂 (replace) = use your hands to swap things.
vocabulary.etymology: From 扌 (hand radical) and 奂 (huàn, which implies 'change' or 'replace'). Directly suggests an action performed by hand to replace something.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng huàn yī jiàn dà hào de.
examples.english: I want to change to a larger size.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ huàn diǎn líng qián ma?
examples.english: Can you give me change for this bill?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for swapping items, changing clothes, exchanging money, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 扌 (hand) + 卓 (tall) = something tall falls from your hands.
vocabulary.etymology: From 扌 (hand radical) and 卓 (zhuó, meaning 'eminent' or 'tall'). Possibly evoking the idea of something eminent/significant falling from the hand.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo xīn, bié bǎ shǒu jī diào le.
examples.english: Be careful, don't drop your phone.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de bǐ diào dào dì shàng le.
examples.english: My pen fell on the floor.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also used as a resultative complement (V+掉) meaning 'off' or 'away' (e.g., 扔掉 'throw away').

vocabulary.mnemonic: 扌 (hand) + 非 (not, negative) = hands pushing things apart to arrange them in a line.
vocabulary.etymology: From 扌 (hand radical) and 非 (fēi, originally depicting two wings opposite each other). The idea is of arranging things by hand side-by-side or in opposition.
vocabulary.measure_word: 排 (pái) is also a measure word for rows.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ yǐ zi pái chéng yī pái.
examples.english: Please line up the chairs in a row.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men zuò zài zuì hòu yī pái.
examples.english: We are sitting in the last row.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb, it means to arrange in a line. As a noun, it means 'a row.'

vocabulary.mnemonic: 排 (line up) + 球 (ball) = a game where players line up to hit a ball.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound noun. 排 (pái) refers to the formation or 'volley' (as in a line of players), and 球 (qiú) means 'ball.'

measure_word.example: 一个排球 (yī gè pái qiú)

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men xià wǔ qù dǎ pái qiú ba.
examples.english: Let's go play volleyball this afternoon.

examples.pinyin: Tā pái qiú dǎ de tè bié hǎo.
examples.english: She plays volleyball really well.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The verb for playing volleyball is 打排球.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 排 (line up) + 队 (team/line) = double emphasis on forming a line with others.
vocabulary.etymology: Verb-Object Compound. 排 (pái) means 'to arrange in a line,' and 队 (duì) means 'a team' or 'a line.' Literally 'to arrange into a line.'

examples.pinyin: Qǐng dà jiā pái duì shàng chē.
examples.english: Please line up to get on the bus.

examples.pinyin: Mǎi nǎi chá yào pái duì ma?
examples.english: Do I need to queue for milk tea?

vocabulary.usage_notes: The quintessential phrase for 'to queue.'

vocabulary.english: to receive, to pick up, to connect
vocabulary.mnemonic: 扌 (hand) + 妾 (concubine) -> historically, a woman received into a household. Now means to receive or connect.
vocabulary.etymology: From 扌 (hand radical) and 妾 (qiè, concubine). The original meaning involved receiving someone (like a bride) into one's household or hands.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù jī chǎng jiē péng you.
examples.english: I'm going to the airport to pick up a friend.

examples.pinyin: Wéi? Wǒ jiē bù dào nǐ de diàn huà.
examples.english: Hello? I can't receive your call.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very versatile: pick up people, answer calls, receive things, or connect parts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 接 (connect) + 下来 (come down) = what comes down to connect to now is what's NEXT.
vocabulary.etymology: A phrase built from 接 (to connect) and the directional complement 下来 (down/coming). Means 'the part that connects/comes next.'

examples.pinyin: Jiē xià lái wǒ men qù nǎ ér?
examples.english: Where are we going next?

examples.pinyin: Jiē xià lái gāi nǐ fā yán le.
examples.english: It's your turn to speak next.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used to transition to the next topic or action in a sequence.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 接 (receive) + 到 (arrive) = the receiving is complete and it has arrived.
vocabulary.etymology: Verb-Resultative Compound. 接 means 'to receive,' and 到 indicates successful completion or arrival.

examples.chinese: 我接到一个奇怪的电话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiē dào yī gè qí guài de diàn huà.
examples.english: I received a strange phone call.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ jiē dào wǒ de yóu jiàn le ma?
examples.english: Did you get my email?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used for receiving calls, messages, or tangible items that have arrived.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 接 (receive into hands) + 受 (receive) = double 'receiving' means fully accepting.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of two verbs with similar meanings: 接 (jiē, to receive) and 受 (shòu, to receive/endure). Emphasizes receiving something willingly.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiē shòu nǐ de dào qiàn.
examples.english: I accept your apology.

examples.pinyin: Tā bù xiǎng jiē shòu bāng zhù.
examples.english: He doesn't want to accept help.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Implies mental or emotional acceptance, not just physical receipt.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 接 (connect) + 着 (continuous aspect) = continuously connecting to what came before.
vocabulary.etymology: 从动词 接 (to connect) 加助词 着 (indicating continuous action)演变而来，表示动作或状态的延续。

examples.chinese: 他讲完了，接着是我发言。
examples.pinyin: Tā jiǎng wán le, jiē zhe shì wǒ fā yán.
examples.english: He finished speaking, then it was my turn to speak.

examples.pinyin: Bié tíng, jiē zhe zuò!
examples.english: Don't stop, carry on!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to indicate the next action in a sequence or to continue an action without interruption.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 扌 (hand) + 隹 (bird) = imagine pushing a bird away with your hands.
vocabulary.etymology: From 扌 (hand radical) and 隹 (zhuī, a short-tailed bird). The connection is unclear but may relate to the action of pushing something away.

examples.pinyin: Bāng wǒ tuī yī xià mén.
examples.english: Help me push the door.

examples.pinyin: Bié tuī wǒ!
examples.english: Don't push me!

vocabulary.usage_notes: The opposite of 拉 (lā, to pull).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 扌 (hand) + 是 (is) = use your hand to lift something up, or bring a topic 'up' in conversation.
vocabulary.etymology: From 扌 (hand radical) and 是 (shì, 'to be,' but here likely a phonetic component). The core meaning involves raising something by hand.

examples.chinese: 这个箱子太重了，我提不动。
examples.pinyin: Zhè gè xiāng zi tài zhòng le, wǒ tí bù dòng.
examples.english: This suitcase is too heavy, I can't lift it.

examples.pinyin: Bié zài huì shàng tí zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: Don't mention this at the meeting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Has both physical ('lift') and abstract ('mention') meanings.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 提 (lift up) + 出 (out) = lift an idea out into the open.
vocabulary.etymology: Verb-Directional Compound. 提 means 'to lift/mention,' and 出 means 'out.' Literally 'to lift out.'

examples.chinese: 他提出了一个很好的建议。
examples.pinyin: Tā tí chū le yī gè hěn hǎo de jiàn yì.
examples.english: He proposed a very good suggestion.

examples.pinyin: Shéi tí chū de zhè gè wèn tí?
examples.english: Who brought up this issue?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used for raising questions, suggestions, or opinions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 提 (mention) + 到 (arrive) = your words 'arrive at' the topic you mention.
vocabulary.etymology: Verb-Resultative Compound. 提 means 'to lift/mention,' and 到 indicates arrival at a point (the topic).

examples.pinyin: Tā gāng cái tí dào le nǐ.
examples.english: He just mentioned you.

examples.chinese: 报告里提到了这个问题。
examples.pinyin: Bào gào lǐ tí dào le zhè gè wèn tí.
examples.english: The report mentioned this issue.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Specifically means 'to make reference to' something or someone.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a hand (攵) closing around a hook (丩) to gather things in.
vocabulary.etymology: The character 收 combines 丩 (jiū, representing entanglement) with 攵 (a hand holding a stick, implying action). The idea is to gather or collect things together.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān shōu le hěn duō kuài dì.
examples.english: I received a lot of packages today.

examples.pinyin: Gāi shōu yī fu le.
examples.english: It's time to bring in the laundry.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often implies gathering in or bringing something to a conclusion (收工).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 收 (collect) + 入 (enter) = money that enters your collection.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound noun. 收 (shōu) means 'to collect,' and 入 (rù) means 'to enter.' Literally 'what is collected and enters.'

measure_word.example: 一份收入 (yī fèn shōu rù)

examples.pinyin: Tā de yuè shōu rù hěn gāo.
examples.english: His monthly income is very high.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì gōng sī de zhǔ yào shōu rù.
examples.english: This is the company's main revenue.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to money earned, typically on a regular basis.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 收 (receive) + 到 (arrive) = the receiving process is complete.
vocabulary.etymology: Verb-Resultative Compound. 收 means 'to receive/collect,' and 到 indicates successful completion or arrival.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shōu dào nǐ de duǎn xìn le.
examples.english: I received your text message.

examples.pinyin: Lǐ wù shōu dào le, xiè xiè nǐ!
examples.english: I've received the gift, thank you!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common confirmation phrase for emails, messages, packages, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 己 (self) + 攵 (hand with stick) = use a stick to correct your own (己) work.
vocabulary.etymology: From 己 (jǐ, self) and 攵 (a hand holding a stick, implying action). The idea is to take action on oneself or one's work to alter it.

examples.chinese: 我需要改一下这个时间。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xū yào gǎi yī xià zhè gè shí jiān.
examples.english: I need to change this time.

examples.chinese: 老师让我改作业里的错误。
examples.pinyin: Lǎo shī ràng wǒ gǎi zuò yè lǐ de cuò wù.
examples.english: The teacher asked me to correct the mistakes in my homework.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for making corrections, alterations, or changes to something existing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 放 (put) + 下 (down) = literally 'put down.'
vocabulary.etymology: Verb-Directional Compound. 放 (fàng) means 'to release' or 'to put,' and 下 (xià) means 'down.'

examples.pinyin: Bǎ xiāng zi fàng xià ba, tài zhòng le.
examples.english: Put the box down, it's too heavy.

examples.chinese: 放下手机，休息一下眼睛。
examples.pinyin: Fàng xià shǒu jī, xiū xī yī xià yǎn jīng.
examples.english: Put down your phone and rest your eyes.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used literally (放下东西) or figuratively (放下烦恼 'let go of worries').

vocabulary.mnemonic: 故 (old) + 事 (matter/affair) = an old affair, a tale from the past.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound noun. 故 (gù) means 'old' or 'former,' and 事 (shì) means 'event' or 'matter.' Literally 'an old event.'

measure_word.example: 一个故事 (yī gè gù shì)

examples.chinese: 妈妈给我讲了一个故事。
examples.pinyin: Mā ma gěi wǒ jiǎng le yī gè gù shì.
examples.english: Mom told me a story.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yī gè ài qíng gù shì.
examples.english: This is a love story.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to narratives, whether fictional, historical, or personal.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 故 (old, as in 'reason') + 意 (intention) = with an old/prior intention, premeditated.
vocabulary.etymology: Compound of 故 (gù, meaning 'cause' or 'reason' in this context) and 意 (yì, meaning 'intention'). Means 'with prior intent.'

examples.pinyin: Tā bù shì gù yì de, bié shēng qì.
examples.english: He didn't do it on purpose, don't be angry.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì gù yì chí dào de ma?
examples.english: Were you deliberately late?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to describe actions done with conscious intent, often implying the outcome was foreseeable.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of '坐' (zuò) meaning 'to sit', so a 座位 is the spot where you SIT down.
vocabulary.etymology: 座 combines 广 (building) with 坐 (to sit), originally meaning a seat or base. 位 means position or place.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen zhǎo gè zuòwèi zuò xià ba.
examples.english: Let's find a seat and sit down.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè zuòwèi yǒu rén ma?
examples.english: Is this seat taken?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common and polite question is 请问，这里有人吗？(Is anyone sitting here?).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a school gate 开 (kāi)ing for the new 学 (xué) term.
vocabulary.etymology: 开 means to open or start. 学 means to learn or school. Together it literally means 'to open school'.

examples.pinyin: Xià zhōuyī wǒmen kāixué.
examples.english: Our school term starts next Monday.

examples.pinyin: Kāixué le, yòu yào zǎo qǐ le.
examples.english: School's starting, time to wake up early again.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with '了' to indicate the event has occurred or is about to occur.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your heart (心) opens (开) up when you're happy.
vocabulary.etymology: 开 means to open or be open. 心 means heart. An open heart signifies happiness and joy.

examples.pinyin: Jīntiān wán de hěn kāixīn!
examples.english: I had a lot of fun today!

examples.pinyin: Kàn dào nǐ wǒ hěn kāixīn.
examples.english: I'm very happy to see you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in spoken Chinese. You can also say 玩得开心 (Have fun!).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You press the button to 开 (open/start) your 机 (machine).
vocabulary.etymology: 开 means to open or start. 机 is short for 机器 (machine) or 手机 (phone).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī kāi bù liǎo jī le.
examples.english: My phone won't turn on.

examples.pinyin: Qǐng xiān kāijī zài dēnglù.
examples.english: Please power on first, then log in.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used specifically for electronics like computers, phones, TVs. The opposite is 关机.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A super useful verb for 'doing' stuff, like fiddling with things. Imagine '弄'ing around.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted two hands (廾) holding jade (玉), implying handling or playing with something. Now a very broad action verb.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒujī nòng diū le.
examples.english: I lost my phone.

examples.chinese: 你能帮我弄一下这个吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng bāng wǒ nòng yīxià zhège ma?
examples.english: Can you help me fix/handle this?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very casual, all-purpose verb. Can mean to do, get, make, fix, handle, or mess up, depending on context.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of it as the verb for 'acting AS' something (当老师) or marking a moment in time (当...的时候).
vocabulary.etymology: The traditional form 當 combines 田 (field) with尚 (esteem), related to managing or matching. Simplified form uses 当.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiějie dāng lǎoshī.
examples.english: My older sister is a teacher.

examples.chinese: 当我有空的时候给你打电话。
examples.pinyin: Dāng wǒ yǒu kòng de shíhòu gěi nǐ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.english: I'll call you when I'm free.

vocabulary.usage_notes: As a verb, it means 'to serve as'. As a preposition, it's often in the pattern 当...的时候 (when...).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 当 (at) that specific 时 (time).
vocabulary.etymology: 当 means to be/at. 时 means time. Together meaning 'at that time'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dāngshí bù zhīdào.
examples.english: I didn't know at that time.

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen dāngshí zài Shànghǎi.
examples.english: We were in Shanghai at the time.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to a specific past time already mentioned in the conversation. Often used in storytelling.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 影 (shadow/image) 片 (piece) — a piece of moving images.
vocabulary.etymology: 影 means shadow or image. 片 means a flat piece or slice. Together it means a film reel or video.

examples.pinyin: Zhè bù yǐngpiàn hěn hǎokàn.
examples.english: This movie is very good.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xǐhuan kàn dònghuà yǐngpiàn.
examples.english: I like watching animated films.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more formal than 电影. Also commonly used for video clips.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It points the direction you're going 往. Think of an arrow.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts a foot (止 variant) on a road, indicating movement toward a place.

examples.pinyin: Wǎng qián zǒu, ránhòu zuǒ zhuǎn.
examples.english: Go straight ahead, then turn left.

examples.pinyin: Zhè tàng huǒchē wǎng Běijīng kāi.
examples.english: This train is heading to Beijing.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Comes before the direction or destination. 往 + direction (e.g., 往左, 往前) or 往 + place.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of it as the verb for getting a 得 (score) on a test. Or the particle that links verbs and descriptions (跑得快).
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted a hand (寸) taking a seashell (貝), which was currency, meaning to obtain.

examples.pinyin: Tā dé le dì yī míng.
examples.english: He got first place.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ Zhōngwén shuō de zhēn hǎo.
examples.english: You speak Chinese really well.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 1) Verb: to get/obtain. 2) Particle: Used after a verb to introduce a complement of degree or manner (e.g., Verb + 得 + Adj).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You 得 (get) something 出 (out) of your thinking — you reach a conclusion.
vocabulary.etymology: 得 means to obtain. 出 means to come out. To obtain something that comes out (of thought).

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen déchūle yīgè jiélùn.
examples.english: We reached a conclusion.

examples.chinese: 从数据中得不出这个答案。
examples.pinyin: Cóng shùjù zhōng dé bù chū zhège dá'àn.
examples.english: You can't derive this answer from the data.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used with abstract results like 结论 (conclusion), 答案 (answer), 结果 (result).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's right in the 中 (middle) of your 心 (heart).
vocabulary.etymology: 心 means heart. 中 means middle or within. Together it means 'within the heart'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīnzhōng yīzhí yǒu gè mèngxiǎng.
examples.english: I've always had a dream in my heart.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒngyuǎn zài wǒ xīnzhōng.
examples.english: You are forever in my heart.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Slightly more literary or emotional than 心里. Often used for deep feelings, beliefs, or memories.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Your heart's (心) emotional weather or 情 (feeling).
vocabulary.etymology: 心 means heart. 情 means feeling or emotion. The condition of the heart's feelings.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīntiān xīnqíng bù hǎo.
examples.english: I'm in a bad mood today.

examples.pinyin: Tīng yīnyuè kěyǐ gǎishàn xīnqíng.
examples.english: Listening to music can improve your mood.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common. You can ask someone 你心情怎么样？ (How are you feeling?).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something inside your 心 (heart) 里 (inside).
vocabulary.etymology: 心 means heart. 里 means inside. Together meaning 'inside the heart'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xīnli hěn nánguò.
examples.english: I feel very sad inside.

examples.chinese: 别把话都放在心里，说出来吧。
examples.pinyin: Bié bǎ huà dōu fàng zài xīnli, shuō chūlái ba.
examples.english: Don't keep everything to yourself, say it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The most common spoken word for 'in one's heart/mind'. Used for thoughts and feelings you keep inside.

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's 必 (inevitable) that you 须 (must) do it. No choice.
vocabulary.etymology: 必 originally meant a handle of a weapon, later used for 'certainly'. 须 means beard/whiskers, later used for 'must' (necessity).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ bìxū zài bā diǎn qián dào jiā.
examples.english: You must be home before eight o'clock.

examples.chinese: 想学好中文必须多练习。
examples.pinyin: Xiǎng xué hǎo Zhōngwén bìxū duō liànxí.
examples.english: To learn Chinese well, you must practice more.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Expresses strong necessity or obligation. Stronger than 需要 (to need).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 快 (fast) + 点儿 (a little) = Be a little faster!
vocabulary.etymology: 快 means fast/quick. 点儿 is the erhua (儿) form of 点, meaning 'a little' or making it more casual.

examples.pinyin: Kuài diǎn r, wǒmen yào chídào le!
examples.english: Hurry up, we're going to be late!

examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng kuài diǎn r chī ma?
examples.english: Can you eat a bit faster?

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common and casual催促 (urge). Often used among friends and family.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Things are getting 快 (fast) and are just 要 (about) to happen.
vocabulary.etymology: 快 means quickly. 要 means will/going to. Together it indicates imminent action.

examples.pinyin: Diànyǐng kuàiyào kāishǐ le.
examples.english: The movie is about to start.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ kuàiyào è sǐ le.
examples.english: I'm about to starve to death.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before a verb to indicate something will happen very soon. Almost always followed by '了'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 快 (fast) 餐 (meal) = a fast meal.
vocabulary.etymology: 快 means fast. 餐 means meal. A meal that is fast.

examples.pinyin: Zhōngwǔ wǒmen chī kuàicān ba.
examples.english: Let's have fast food for lunch.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā kuàicān diàn hěn piányi.
examples.english: This fast food restaurant is very cheap.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to Western fast food (KFC, McDonald's) or Chinese-style quick meals.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Something happens so fast it makes you say '忽?!' (Huh?!) 然 (then).
vocabulary.etymology: 忽 originally meant to neglect or be careless, implying something overlooked that appears suddenly. 然 is a suffix meaning 'state of'.

examples.pinyin: Tiān hūrán xià qǐle dàyǔ.
examples.english: It suddenly started pouring.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ hūrán xiǎng qǐlái le.
examples.english: It suddenly came to my mind.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used before the verb. Very similar to 突然, but 突然 can also be an adjective.

vocabulary.mnemonic: You're in a tough spot and ask '怎么 (how) 办 (handle) this?'
vocabulary.etymology: 怎么 means how. 办 means to handle or do. Literally 'how to handle?'

examples.pinyin: Wǒ de yàoshi diū le, zěnme bàn?
examples.english: I lost my keys, what should I do?

examples.pinyin: Bié zháojí, zǒng huì yǒu bànfǎ de.
examples.english: Don't panic, there will always be a way.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A universal phrase for asking for solutions when facing a problem. Often shows worry or panic.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of it as asking about the 样 (appearance/manner) of something — 怎么 (how) is its 样?
vocabulary.etymology: 怎 is a question word for 'how'. 样 means appearance, manner, or kind. Together it asks about the state or manner.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ juéde zhè bù diànyǐng zěnyàng?
examples.english: What do you think of this movie?

examples.pinyin: Wǒmen míngtiān zěnyàng jiànmiàn?
examples.english: How shall we meet tomorrow?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Interchangeable with 怎么样. Can be used to ask for an opinion or for a method.

vocabulary.english: to be afraid of, to fear
vocabulary.mnemonic: Your heart (忄) feels white (白) with fear.
vocabulary.etymology: 心忄 (heart) + 白 (white). A white heart was associated with timidity or a sudden fright.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ mèimei pà gǒu.
examples.english: My younger sister is afraid of dogs.

examples.pinyin: Bié pà, wǒ zài zhèr.
examples.english: Don't be afraid, I'm here.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Also used to express worry, as in 我怕迟到 (I'm worried about being late).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine your heart (心) feeling rushed and under a tight schedule — it's an 急 situation.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts a hand (刍) gripping a heart (心), conveying a sense of urgency or anxiety.

examples.pinyin: Bié jí, wǒmen hái yǒu shíjiān.
examples.english: Don't rush, we still have time.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu jí shì, xiān zǒu le.
examples.english: I have something urgent, I have to go.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can describe a person's mood (着急) or a situation (急事).

vocabulary.english: to think of, to occur to
vocabulary.mnemonic: You 想 (think) and the idea arrives/到 (reaches) your mind.
vocabulary.etymology: 想 means to think. 到 means to arrive or reach. An idea reaches your thoughts.

examples.chinese: 我刚刚想到一个好主意。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ gānggāng xiǎng dào yīgè hǎo zhǔyì.
examples.english: I just thought of a good idea.

examples.pinyin: Kàn dào dàngāo, wǒ jiù xiǎng dào nǐ.
examples.english: Seeing cake reminds me of you.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used when a thought or memory comes to mind spontaneously.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 法 (way/method) that comes from your 想 (thinking).
vocabulary.etymology: 想 means to think. 法 means method or way. The way/method of thinking, i.e., an idea.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ yǒu shénme hǎo xiǎngfǎ?
examples.english: Do you have any good ideas?

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǐ shì wǒ de gèrén xiǎngfǎ.
examples.english: This is just my personal opinion.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be a concrete idea or a general opinion. 我有一个想法 = I have an idea.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of 'small talk' -> a story made up from small words.
vocabulary.etymology: 小 (small, trivial) + 说 (speech, talk). Historically referred to trivial or unofficial talk/stories.

measure_word.example: 一本小说 (yì běn xiǎo shuō)

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zuì xǐ huān kàn kē huàn xiǎo shuō.
examples.english: I love reading science fiction novels.

examples.pinyin: Zhè běn xiǎo shuō xiě de tài hǎo le!
examples.english: This novel is written so well!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can refer to any fictional story, short or long.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Few (少) years of life.
vocabulary.etymology: 少 (few, little, young) + 年 (year). Literally 'young years'.

measure_word.example: 一个少年 (yí gè shào nián)

examples.pinyin: Tā shì gè ài yùn dòng de shào nián.
examples.english: He is a sports-loving teenager.

examples.pinyin: Shào nián shí dài zǒng shì hěn nán wàng.
examples.english: The teenage years are always unforgettable.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often implies a male adolescent, but can be generic.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Count the numbers that are few.
vocabulary.etymology: 少 (few, little) + 数 (number, count). Literally 'few number'.

examples.chinese: 只有少数人知道这件事。
examples.pinyin: Zhǐ yǒu shǎo shù rén zhī dào zhè jiàn shì.
examples.english: Only a small number of people know about this.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men shì shǎo shù pài.
examples.english: We are the minority faction.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often contrasted with 多数 (majority).

vocabulary.mnemonic: It's 'just' (就) what you 'want' (要) to happen next.
vocabulary.etymology: 就 (precisely, just) + 要 (want, will). Together they express imminent action.

examples.pinyin: Diàn yǐng jiù yào kāi shǐ le.
examples.english: The movie is about to start.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiù yào chū mén le, děng deng wǒ!
examples.english: I'm about to leave, wait for me!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used with 了 (le) to indicate an imminent change of state.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Piles of things, like layers of a cake.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 層. The original character depicted a house with multiple storeys.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ zhù zài wǔ céng.
examples.english: I live on the fifth floor.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè dàn gāo yǒu sān céng.
examples.english: This cake has three layers.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A measure word for layers, floors, and tiers. For building floors, 楼 is also common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The difference is so little it 'almost' doesn't exist.
vocabulary.etymology: 差 (difference) + 不 (not) + 多 (much). Literally 'the difference is not much'.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men chà bu duō gāo.
examples.english: We are almost the same height.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ chà bu duō zhǔn bèi hǎo le.
examples.english: I'm almost ready.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in speech. Can express approximation or that something is 'good enough'.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A place with a lot of business and noise.
vocabulary.etymology: Depicts a marketplace, historically a place for trading.

examples.pinyin: Běi jīng shì yí gè hěn dà de shì.
examples.english: Beijing is a very big city.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ qù cài shì mǎi diǎn dōng xi.
examples.english: I'm going to the vegetable market to buy some things.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often part of city names (上海市) and compound words.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The 'long' (leader) of the city.
vocabulary.etymology: 市 (city) + 长 (chief, leader, head).

measure_word.example: 一位市长 (yí wèi shì zhǎng)

examples.pinyin: Xīn shì zhǎng hěn nián qīng.
examples.english: The new mayor is very young.

examples.chinese: 市长今天会来我们学校。
examples.pinyin: Shì zhǎng jīn tiān huì lái wǒ men xué xiào.
examples.english: The mayor will come to our school today.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Bring it and make it arrive here.
vocabulary.etymology: 带 (to bring, to carry) + 来 (to come). Verb-complement structure.

examples.chinese: 你能给我带杯咖啡来吗？
examples.pinyin: Nǐ néng gěi wǒ dài bēi kā fēi lái ma?
examples.english: Can you bring me a coffee?

examples.pinyin: Zhè chǎng yǔ dài lái le hǎo tiān qì.
examples.english: This rain has brought good weather.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Focuses on the action of bringing something towards the speaker or to a location. The opposite is 带走 (take away).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Used all the time, like your everyday routine.
vocabulary.etymology: 常 (often, constant) + 用 (to use).

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì wǒ cháng yòng de mì mǎ.
examples.english: This is my commonly used password.

examples.pinyin: Zhè gè cí bù cháng yòng.
examples.english: This word is not commonly used.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often precedes a noun it modifies (常用的词).

vocabulary.mnemonic: You see it often because it's everywhere.
vocabulary.etymology: 常 (often) + 见 (to see). Literally 'often seen'.

examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè cháng jiàn de wèn tí.
examples.english: This is a common problem.

examples.chinese: 这种鸟在我们这儿很常见。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhǒng niǎo zài wǒ men zhè er hěn cháng jiàn.
examples.english: This kind of bird is very common here.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Similar to 常用 but focuses on observation/frequency of occurrence, not usage.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Dry your cup!
vocabulary.etymology: 干 (dry, do) + 杯 (cup, glass). Means to empty/dry your cup.

examples.pinyin: Wèi le wǒ men de chéng gōng, gān bēi!
examples.english: To our success, cheers!

examples.pinyin: Lái, dà jiā yì qǐ gān bēi!
examples.english: Come on, everyone cheers together!

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common toast. Often said while clinking glasses.

vocabulary.english: to work, to do manual labor
vocabulary.mnemonic: Do work (干 + 活儿).
vocabulary.etymology: 干 (to do) + 活儿 (erhua form of 活, work, job). Colloquial compound.

examples.pinyin: Bà ba zài huā yuán lǐ gàn huó r.
examples.english: Dad is working in the garden.

examples.pinyin: Gàn le yì tiān huó r, zhēn lèi.
examples.english: I've worked all day, I'm really tired.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very casual, often for physical or hands-on work. Note pronunciation: gàn huór.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A line that's perfectly straight and even.
vocabulary.etymology: Pictograph of a balanced and level object.

examples.pinyin: Zhè zhāng zhuō zi hěn píng.
examples.english: This table is very flat.

examples.pinyin: Tā xiàn zài xīn qíng hěn píng.
examples.english: He is feeling very calm now.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A core character with many compound words. Can describe surfaces, situations, or emotions.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Flat and safe, no bumps in the road of life.
vocabulary.etymology: 平 (flat, calm) + 安 (peace, safe). Together meaning peaceful and safe.

examples.pinyin: Zhù nǐ yí lù píng ān!
examples.english: Have a safe journey!

examples.pinyin: Zhǐ yào jiā rén píng ān jiù hǎo.
examples.english: As long as the family is safe and sound, that's all that matters.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Common in greetings and good wishes, especially for travel (一路平安).

vocabulary.mnemonic: The flat and constant routine.
vocabulary.etymology: 平 (ordinary, flat) + 常 (often, constant). Describes the usual state.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ píng cháng qī diǎn qǐ chuáng.
examples.english: I usually get up at seven.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān shì gè píng cháng de rì zi.
examples.english: Today is an ordinary day.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be used as a time adverb (normally) or an adjective (ordinary). Interchangeable with 平时 in many contexts.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The flat, usual time.
vocabulary.etymology: 平 (ordinary) + 时 (time). Literally 'ordinary time'.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ píng shí xǐ huān zuò shén me?
examples.english: What do you usually like to do?

examples.pinyin: Tā píng shí bù hē jiǔ.
examples.english: He doesn't usually drink.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Almost identical to 平常. Often used as a time adverbial.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A level and balanced scale for everyone.
vocabulary.etymology: 平 (level, fair) + 等 (rank, grade). Literally 'level rank'.

examples.pinyin: Fǎ lǜ miàn qián rén rén píng děng.
examples.english: All people are equal before the law.

examples.chinese: 我们应该追求性别平等。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ men yīng gāi zhuī qiú xìng bié píng děng.
examples.english: We should pursue gender equality.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A key social and political concept.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Which year's class are you in?
vocabulary.etymology: 年 (year) + 级 (level, grade). The level based on years of study.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ dì di zài sān nián jí.
examples.english: My younger brother is in third grade.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ shì jǐ nián jí de xué sheng?
examples.english: What grade are you in?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for primary and secondary school grades. University levels use 大一, 大二, etc.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Few years, light in age.
vocabulary.etymology: 年 (year) + 轻 (light, not heavy). Figuratively 'light in years'.

examples.chinese: 她还很年轻，有很多机会。
examples.pinyin: Tā hái hěn nián qīng, yǒu hěn duō jī huì.
examples.english: She is still very young and has many opportunities.

examples.pinyin: Nián qīng zhēn hǎo!
examples.english: Being young is great!

vocabulary.usage_notes: Describes people, or things metaphorically (e.g., a young company).

vocabulary.mnemonic: Widely broadcast to tell you about something.
vocabulary.etymology: 广 (broad, wide) + 告 (to tell, to announce). Literally 'wide announcement'.

measure_word.example: 一个广告 (yí gè guǎng gào)

examples.pinyin: Diàn shì shàng de guǎng gào tài duō le.
examples.english: There are too many ads on TV.

examples.chinese: 我在网上看到这个广告。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ zài wǎng shàng kàn dào zhè gè guǎng gào.
examples.english: I saw this ad online.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A wide, open place where people gather.
vocabulary.etymology: 广 (broad, wide) + 场 (field, open space). Literally 'wide field'.

measure_word.example: 一个广场 (yí gè guǎng chǎng)

examples.chinese: 晚上很多人去广场跳舞。
examples.pinyin: Wǎn shàng hěn duō rén qù guǎng chǎng tiào wǔ.
examples.english: Many people go to the square to dance in the evening.

examples.pinyin: Tiān ān mén guǎng chǎng hěn dà.
examples.english: Tiananmen Square is very big.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used in place names (人民广场).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A place under a roof where you stand and buy things.
vocabulary.etymology: Simplified from 店. Originally meant an inn or a shop.

examples.pinyin: Qián miàn yǒu yì jiā kā fēi diàn.
examples.english: There's a coffee shop ahead.

examples.pinyin: Zhè jiā diàn de dōng xi hěn pián yi.
examples.english: This shop's things are very cheap.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A very common word for all kinds of retail shops.

vocabulary.mnemonic: A measure of how much, like on a thermometer.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally related to measuring and law. Now used for units of measurement.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān sān shí dù, hěn rè.
examples.english: It's thirty degrees today, very hot.

examples.chinese: 他工作很认真，有一定程度。
examples.pinyin: Tā gōng zuò hěn rèn zhēn, yǒu yí dìng chéng dù.
examples.english: He works very diligently, to a certain extent.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A key measure word for angles, temperature, and electricity. Also used in abstract nouns (程度).

vocabulary.mnemonic: A large, solid object you can sit on or that sits there.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally depicted two people sitting back-to-back on the ground.

examples.pinyin: Jiào shì lǐ yǒu hěn duō zuò.
examples.english: There are many seats in the classroom.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā fù jìn yǒu yí zuò gōng yuán.
examples.english: There is a park near my home.

vocabulary.usage_notes: A common measure word for large, fixed objects like mountains, bridges, buildings, and cities.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Sounds like "how many" but it's "好" (good) + "多" (many) = a good many!
vocabulary.etymology: 好 (good) + 多 (many). It literally combines the concepts of 'good' and 'many' to express a pleasingly large quantity.

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān wǒ mǎi le hǎo duō shuǐ guǒ.
examples.english: Today I bought a lot of fruit.

examples.pinyin: Wài miàn yǒu hǎo duō rén.
examples.english: There are a lot of people outside.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Very common in spoken Chinese. It often implies the quantity is more than expected or is pleasantly large.

vocabulary.mnemonic: The character has 女 (woman/female) + 生 (birth), think of family names passed down from birth.
vocabulary.etymology: Composed of 女 (woman) and 生 (to give birth). Historically, it relates to the matrilineal origins of Chinese surnames.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xìng shén me?
examples.english: What is your family name?

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xìng Wáng.
examples.english: My surname is Wang.

vocabulary.usage_notes: When asking for someone's full name, you usually ask 你叫什么名字？ 你姓什么？ specifically asks for the family name.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 姓 (surname) + 名 (given name) = the complete name tag.
vocabulary.etymology: A compound of 姓 (family name) and 名 (given name).

examples.chinese: 请在这里填写您的姓名。
examples.pinyin: Qǐng zài zhè lǐ tián xiě nín de xìng míng.
examples.english: Please write your full name here.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ bù zhī dào tā de xìng míng.
examples.english: I don't know his full name.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used in formal contexts like forms, registrations, or official introductions. In daily chat, 名字 is more common.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 字 (character) + 典 (canon) = the canon of characters.
vocabulary.etymology: 字 (character, word) + 典 (standard work, canon). It refers specifically to a reference book for Chinese characters.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jīng cháng yòng shǒu jī chá zì diǎn.
examples.english: I often use my phone to look up characters in a dictionary.

examples.chinese: 这本字典是老师给我的。
examples.pinyin: Zhè běn zì diǎn shì lǎo shī gěi wǒ de.
examples.english: This dictionary was given to me by my teacher.

vocabulary.usage_notes: 字典 is for characters; 词典 is for words and phrases. Both are often called "dictionary" in English.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 学 (study) + 期 (period) = the study period.
vocabulary.etymology: 学 (to study, learning) + 期 (period of time).

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xué qī nǐ yǒu jǐ mén kè?
examples.english: How many classes do you have this semester?

examples.pinyin: Xià xué qī wǒ yào qù shí xí.
examples.english: Next semester I'm going to do an internship.

vocabulary.mnemonic: Think of a pet: "Tā" is for pets and objects, not people.
vocabulary.etymology: Originally written as 佗, a variant of 他. It was differentiated later to specifically refer to non-human things.

examples.chinese: 我的手机呢？你看见它了吗？
examples.pinyin: Wǒ de shǒu jī ne? Nǐ kàn jiàn tā le ma?
examples.english: Where's my phone? Have you seen it?

examples.chinese: 这只猫很可爱，我喜欢它。
examples.pinyin: Zhè zhī māo hěn kě ài, wǒ xǐ huān tā.
examples.english: This cat is very cute, I like it.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for objects, animals, or ideas. For plural non-human things, use 它们 (tā men).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 它 (it) + 们 (plural marker) = all the "its".
vocabulary.etymology: 它 (it) + 们 (plural suffix for pronouns and some nouns).

examples.chinese: 这些书很重，把它们放在桌子上吧。
examples.pinyin: Zhè xiē shū hěn zhòng, bǎ tā men fàng zài zhuō zi shàng ba.
examples.english: These books are heavy, put them on the table.

examples.chinese: 那些狗在跑，它们很开心。
examples.pinyin: Nà xiē gǒu zài pǎo, tā men hěn kāi xīn.
examples.english: Those dogs are running, they are very happy.

vocabulary.usage_notes: The plural form of 它. Used only for non-human nouns.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 安 (peace) + 全 (complete) = completely at peace = safe.
vocabulary.etymology: 安 (peace, calm) + 全 (complete, whole). It implies being in a state of complete peace and wholeness.

examples.pinyin: Guò mǎ lù yào zhù yì ān quán.
examples.english: Pay attention to safety when crossing the street.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiǎo qū hěn ān quán.
examples.english: This neighborhood is very safe.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Extremely common word. Can be used as a noun (安全第一 - safety first) or adjective (很安全).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 安 (peace) + 静 (still) = peaceful and still = quiet.
vocabulary.etymology: 安 (peace, calm) + 静 (still, quiet).

examples.pinyin: Tú shū guǎn lǐ qǐng bǎo chí ān jìng.
examples.english: Please keep quiet in the library.

examples.chinese: 他需要一个安静的地方工作。
examples.pinyin: Tā xū yào yí gè ān jìng de dì fang gōng zuò.
examples.english: He needs a quiet place to work.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used as a command: 安静！ (Be quiet!). 安静点 is a softer version meaning "Be a little quieter."

vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine a roof (宀) over something completed.
vocabulary.etymology: The original form depicted a person under a roof, suggesting completion or being at home (a finished state).

examples.pinyin: Nǐ zuò yè zuò wán le ma?
examples.english: Have you finished your homework?

examples.pinyin: Diàn yǐng kuài wán le.
examples.english: The movie is almost over.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Usually follows another verb as a result complement (V+完). 做完了 (done doing), 吃完了 (finished eating).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 完 (finish) + 全 (whole) = finished and whole = completely.
vocabulary.etymology: 完 (to finish, complete) + 全 (whole, entire).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ wán quán tóng yì nǐ de kàn fǎ.
examples.english: I completely agree with you.

examples.chinese: 这是一个完全不同的故事。
examples.pinyin: Zhè shì yí gè wán quán bù tóng de gù shi.
examples.english: This is a completely different story.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often used to emphasize totality. It's stronger than 很 (very).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 实 (real) + 习 (practice) = real-world practice.
vocabulary.etymology: 实 (real, solid) + 习 (to practice, to learn). It means putting theory into real practice.

examples.chinese: 我暑假要去一家公司实习。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ shǔ jià yào qù yì jiā gōng sī shí xí.
examples.english: I'm going to intern at a company this summer.

examples.pinyin: Tā de shí xí qī shì sān gè yuè.
examples.english: His internship period is three months.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used by university students. Can be a verb (去实习) or a noun (一份实习).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 实 (real) + 在 (to be at) = being real and present = genuine.
vocabulary.etymology: 实 (real, solid) + 在 (to exist, to be at). It conveys the quality of being genuine and present in reality.

examples.chinese: 他这个人很实在，不会骗人。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhè ge rén hěn shí zài, bù huì piàn rén.
examples.english: He is a very honest person and won't lie.

examples.pinyin: Zhè dùn fàn shí zài tài hǎo chī le!
examples.english: This meal is really delicious!

vocabulary.usage_notes: As an adjective, it describes a person's character (honest, down-to-earth). As an adverb, it emphasizes a statement (really, truly).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 实 (real) + 现 (appear) = make something real appear.
vocabulary.etymology: 实 (real) + 现 (to appear, to manifest).

examples.chinese: 他终于实现了自己的梦想。
examples.pinyin: Tā zhōng yú shí xiàn le zì jǐ de mèng xiǎng.
examples.english: He finally realized his dream.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge jì huà hěn nán shí xiàn.
examples.english: This plan is very hard to achieve.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used for abstract goals, dreams, plans, or wishes becoming reality.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 实 (real) + 际 (border) = the real border/scope of something = the practical facts.
vocabulary.etymology: 实 (real) + 际 (border, edge, occasion). It refers to the real circumstances or practical side of things.

examples.chinese: 实际的情况比我们想的复杂。
examples.pinyin: Shí jì de qíng kuàng bǐ wǒ men xiǎng de fù zá.
examples.english: The actual situation is more complicated than we thought.

examples.pinyin: Zhè ge xiǎng fǎ bú tài shí jì.
examples.english: This idea isn't very practical.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Often contrasts with 理论 (theory). 实际上 (in fact, actually) is a very common phrase.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 客 (guest) + 人 (person) = the guest person.
vocabulary.etymology: 客 (guest, visitor) + 人 (person).

examples.pinyin: Jīn tiān wǎn shàng jiā lǐ yǒu kè rén.
examples.english: We have guests at home tonight.

examples.pinyin: Zhè wèi kè rén xiǎng diǎn cài.
examples.english: This customer would like to order.

vocabulary.usage_notes: In restaurants/stores, it means 'customer'. At home, it means 'guest'. 位 is the polite measure word.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 家 (home) + 庭 (courtyard) = the home and its courtyard = the family unit.
vocabulary.etymology: 家 (home, family) + 庭 (courtyard, hall). It refers to the family as a household unit.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ yǒu yí gè xìng fú de jiā tíng.
examples.english: I have a happy family.

examples.pinyin: Jiā tíng zuò yè zuò wán le ma?
examples.english: Have you finished your homework? (家庭作业 is a common term for homework).

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the family as a social unit. More formal than just 家. 家庭背景 means family background.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 家 (family) + 长 (head/elder) = the head of the family.
vocabulary.etymology: 家 (family) + 长 (head, elder, to grow). It means the head or elder of a family.

examples.pinyin: Míng tiān xué xiào yào kāi jiā zhǎng huì.
examples.english: The school is having a parent-teacher meeting tomorrow.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ shì hái zi de jiā zhǎng.
examples.english: I am the child's parent.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Most commonly used in the context of a child's parents, especially in school settings (家长会).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 对 (mutual) + 话 (speech) = mutual speech.
vocabulary.etymology: 对 (to face, mutual) + 话 (speech, words). It implies a spoken exchange between two or more parties.

examples.chinese: 我想和他进行一次认真的对话。
examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎng hé tā jìn xíng yí cì rèn zhēn de duì huà.
examples.english: I want to have a serious conversation with him.

examples.chinese: 这部电影里的对话很有意思。
examples.pinyin: Zhè bù diàn yǐng lǐ de duì huà hěn yǒu yì si.
examples.english: The dialogue in this movie is very interesting.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Can be formal or informal. As a verb, it's less common in casual speech than 聊天 (to chat).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 对 (face-to-face) + 面 (side/face) = the side that's facing you.
vocabulary.etymology: 对 (to face) + 面 (face, side, surface). It literally means the facing side.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ jiā jiù zài chāo shì duì miàn.
examples.english: My home is right across from the supermarket.

examples.pinyin: Duì miàn zǒu guò lái yí gè rén.
examples.english: A person is walking over from the opposite side.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used to indicate location. Can stand alone (在对面) or follow a noun (超市对面).

vocabulary.english: to seal, measure word for letters
vocabulary.mnemonic: Imagine sealing an envelope with soil (土) under two trees (圭).
vocabulary.etymology: The character depicts adding earth (土) to a boundary, symbolizing sealing or enclosing.

examples.pinyin: Wǒ gěi nǐ xiě le yì fēng xìn.
examples.english: I wrote you a letter. (封 as measure word)

examples.pinyin: Qǐng bǎ píng zi fēng hǎo.
examples.english: Please seal the bottle well. (封 as verb)

vocabulary.usage_notes: Commonly used as a measure word for letters, emails, or sealed documents. As a verb, it means to close or seal something shut.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 小 (small) + 声 (sound) = small sound.
vocabulary.etymology: 小 (small) + 声 (sound, voice).

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo shēng diǎn, hái zi zài shuì jiào.
examples.english: Keep your voice down, the child is sleeping.

examples.pinyin: Tā men zài xiǎo shēng shuō huà.
examples.english: They are speaking in low voices.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Used as an adverb before verbs like 说, 唱, 读. 小声点 is a common request to be quieter.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 小 (small) + 心 (heart) = pay attention with your little heart.
vocabulary.etymology: 小 (small) + 心 (heart, mind). It implies being attentive with a focused mind.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo xīn! Dì shàng yǒu shuǐ.
examples.english: Be careful! There's water on the floor.

examples.pinyin: Tā kāi chē hěn xiǎo xīn.
examples.english: He drives very carefully.

vocabulary.usage_notes: Most often used as a warning or command. Can also describe a person's character (他很小心).

vocabulary.mnemonic: 小 (small) + 时候 (time) = the time when you were small.
vocabulary.etymology: 小 (small, little) + 时候 (time, moment).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ xiǎo shí hou zhù zài Běi jīng.
examples.english: I lived in Beijing when I was little.

examples.pinyin: Nǐ xiǎo shí hou pà hēi ma?
examples.english: Were you afraid of the dark when you were a child?

vocabulary.usage_notes: Refers to the period of being a child. Usually used in stories or reminiscing.

vocabulary.mnemonic: 小 (small) + 组 (organize) = a small organized unit.
vocabulary.etymology: 小 (small) + 组 (to organize, group).

examples.pinyin: Wǒ men fēn chéng le sān gè xiǎo zǔ.
examples.english: We divided into three small groups.

examples.pinyin: Xiǎo zǔ tǎo lùn xiàn zài kāi shǐ.
